questions.stem: Why begin product-based planning with products rather than estimated tasks?
options: Clarifying the deliverables enables better estimates, dependencies and schedules
Tasks are always more important than acceptance criteria
Product definitions remove the need for quality checks
Planning is only needed after project completion
questions.why: Products and their descriptions should drive the subsequent work, effort, dependency and schedule planning.

questions.stem: What should a project product description include?
options: User quality expectations and acceptance criteria for the overall project product
Only the project's planned advertising spend
questions.why: The project product description defines the overall delivered product and how acceptance will be judged.

questions.stem: A predecessor system needs to be operational before data migration can start. What planning concept is illustrated?
questions.why: Dependencies express relationships between activities or products that affect sequencing and scheduling.

questions.stem: An agreed stage plan will no longer be viable due to a forecast exception. What is an appropriate planning response following direction?
options: Prepare an exception plan to replace the relevant plan if requested
Continue the old plan as though nothing changed
Issue only a benefits management approach
questions.why: An exception plan is prepared to show a viable way forward following an exception when the relevant authority requests it.

questions.stem: A team estimates detailed delivery work two years in advance even though requirements remain uncertain. Which guidance is relevant?
options: Planning horizon: plan current work in more detail and later work at a suitable higher level
All stages require equal detail at project initiation
Detail should only be added after closure
Products are irrelevant to near-term planning
questions.why: Planning horizons recognize that near work can be planned more reliably than distant, uncertain work.

questions.stem: Which document identifies a product's specific quality measures and the finished levels that must be achieved?
questions.why: A product description captures quality specifications and relevant quality methods for its product.

questions.stem: A tester checks whether a completed component meets the approved specification. Which activity is this?
questions.why: Quality control evaluates compliance of specific products against their quality specifications.

questions.stem: An independent function checks whether the project's quality system is suitable and being followed. Which concept is this?
options: Quality control of an individual product
questions.why: Quality assurance is generally managed independently and provides confidence that quality requirements will be met.

questions.stem: A final product must satisfy a prioritized set of conditions before the customer accepts it. What are these conditions?
questions.why: Acceptance criteria determine whether the overall project product is acceptable to the user.

questions.stem: A colleague calls any nice-to-have quality preference an approved requirement. What distinction matters?
options: A requirement is a documented need or expectation in an approved management product
Any suggestion becomes a baseline without approval
Requirements and emerging risks are always identical
Only supplier requests count as requirements
questions.why: PRINCE2 distinguishes agreed and documented requirements from general expectations or unapproved suggestions.

questions.stem: The project manager wants an overview of the current delivery status of individual products. What would support this?
questions.why: The product register tracks product status across the project; the quality register tracks quality activities and their results.

questions.stem: The team wants to record scheduled testing, when it happened and its outcome. Which register is appropriate?
questions.why: The quality register records planned and completed quality activities and results.

questions.stem: A product fails an agreed test. What is the next general requirement?
options: Record the result and manage the failure using the agreed quality and issue arrangements
Automatically accept the product because testing was performed
Ignore the result if the project is on time
questions.why: Quality checks create evidence; failures require controlled resolution rather than silent acceptance.

questions.stem: A storm might delay equipment shipment next month. Why is this a risk rather than an issue?
options: It is an uncertain future event that could affect objectives
It has already occurred and needs issue resolution
It is an approved change to the baseline
It is a deliverable awaiting acceptance
questions.why: Risk concerns uncertain events; an issue is an event or concern that requires management consideration.

questions.stem: What distinguishes the risk owner from the risk action owner?
options: The owner manages the whole risk; the action owner performs assigned response actions
The risk action owner alone funds the entire project
Both are automatically the project executive
Only the action owner may record new risks
questions.why: The risk owner monitors and controls overall assigned risk, while an action owner implements particular agreed actions.

questions.stem: A team takes steps to make a favorable uncertain event more likely. Which opportunity response is used?
questions.why: Enhance increases the probability or impact of an opportunity, unlike avoid and reduce which describe typical threat responses.

questions.stem: A project redesigns a solution so a particular threat can no longer occur. Which response is this?
questions.why: Avoiding a threat removes its cause or effect on the project, rather than simply reducing its likelihood.

questions.stem: The board sets the overall amount and type of uncertainty it is willing to pursue. What is this?
questions.why: Risk appetite expresses the organization's willingness to take risk in pursuit of objectives.

questions.stem: What does risk tolerance define?
options: A measurable acceptable threshold for an objective exposed to risk
The minimum number of team managers
The duration of an initiation stage
questions.why: Risk tolerance uses measurable thresholds to bound how much variation is tolerable.

questions.stem: A risk could occur in two weeks and damage service continuity within minutes. Which pairing is correct?
options: Proximity: two weeks; velocity: within minutes
Proximity: within minutes; velocity: two weeks
Both are types of issue report
Both refer only to monetary impact
questions.why: Proximity is how near an uncertain event might occur; velocity is how quickly its effect would be felt once it occurred.

questions.stem: During which risk technique step should the team assess and prioritize identified threats and opportunities?
questions.why: The risk technique identifies risks, assesses them, plans responses, implements actions and communicates throughout.

questions.stem: A customer asks to modify the agreed interface of an approved product. What type of issue is this?
options: Risk that has not yet been identified
questions.why: A proposed amendment to a baselined product is a request for change and follows issue/change control.

questions.stem: A feature will not satisfy its approved quality specification. Which issue type fits best?
questions.why: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its agreed quality specifications.

questions.stem: A system integration failure has happened and is blocking testing. What best describes it?
options: A problem requiring current management action
Only a change to the business case
questions.why: The event has occurred and has negative impact; issue management deals with problems that require action.

questions.stem: A supplier proposes an unexpected improvement that could save operational costs. Which issue type may apply?
questions.why: An unanticipated positive possibility arising during delivery can be managed as a business-opportunity issue.

questions.stem: What is meant by project baseline?
options: The approved versions of controlled project and management products
Any unsigned idea discussed at a meeting
questions.why: Baselined products are the approved current versions against which changes are controlled.

questions.stem: An issue has been logged and the team needs to understand its impact on cost, scope and justification. Which step follows?
options: Skip straight to a new mandate
questions.why: Issue management examines impact before recommending options and authorizing decisions.

questions.stem: A change authority is given a limited budget to authorize small changes. What matters most?
options: Its delegated limits and approved change budget must be observed
It automatically replaces the project board entirely
It can rewrite every project-level tolerance
It cannot approve any change once established
questions.why: Decision rights and change budgets may be delegated subject to agreed constraints.

questions.stem: Which management product captures a significant issue's options, assessment and recommendation?
questions.why: The issue report records a particular significant issue for decision and resolution; the issue register tracks issues across the project.

questions.stem: The project manager has approved a change within delegated authority. What follows in the issue technique?
options: Implement the authorized change and update controlled records
Treat the change as a new uncertain risk only
Ask the senior user to cancel every test
questions.why: Issue management uses capture, assess, recommend, decide and implement; implementation updates the relevant baseline.

questions.stem: A team manager sends a regular work-package status report to the project manager. What is it?
questions.why: Checkpoint reports communicate team/work-package progress to the project manager.

questions.stem: A project manager provides the board with a regular summary of stage status. What is it?
questions.why: Highlight reports are regular summaries of stage status from the project manager to the project board.

questions.stem: At a management-stage boundary the board needs a summary of performance against the stage plan. Which report supports the decision?
questions.why: End stage reports review the stage and inform the board before a decision to proceed.

questions.stem: A tolerance is forecast to be exceeded but has not actually been breached yet. What does PRINCE2 call the situation?
questions.why: An exception is a forecast deviation beyond agreed tolerances; escalation should not wait for actual overspend or delay.

questions.stem: A team manager raises a forecast work-package tolerance breach. To which level should it ordinarily go first?
questions.why: Exception control escalates first to the next appropriate management level for work-package tolerances.

questions.stem: A project manager expects a stage to exceed tolerance. Which report informs the board?
questions.why: An exception report presents the forecast deviation and its implications to the directing level.

questions.stem: Which is an example of an event-driven control?
options: The project board reviewing an end stage report at a stage boundary
Issuing a highlight report every Friday
Checking the team's status each morning
Holding a monthly risk meeting regardless of events
questions.why: Event-driven controls occur at specified events; time-driven controls operate at a regular interval.

questions.stem: Which management product is most useful for recording lessons for later application?
questions.why: The lessons log captures lessons as they emerge, supporting learning during and across projects.

questions.stem: What should a forecast do beyond reporting what happened last week?
options: Estimate future performance against objectives and tolerances
Only copy the previous day's checkpoint report
Guarantee all uncertainties will not occur
questions.why: The progress practice compares actual achievements with plans and forecasts the likely future position.

questions.stem: What should be decided during starting up a project before committing significant initiation resources?
options: Whether the project is sufficiently worthwhile to initiate
Whether every final benefit has already been realized
Whether the final product is accepted
Whether all technical work is complete
questions.why: Starting up assesses whether there is enough justification to invest in initiating the project.

questions.stem: Which process prepares the project initiation documentation and detailed justification?
questions.why: Initiating a project establishes the firm foundations and approaches used to manage the project.

questions.stem: Which process allows the project board to retain strategic direction while delegating day-to-day management?
questions.why: Directing a project is the board's governance process, operating through authorizations and exception decisions.

questions.stem: Which process primarily enables the project manager to assign and monitor work during a stage?
questions.why: Controlling a stage covers assigning work packages, reviewing stage status, dealing with issues and communicating progress.

questions.stem: A team manager has accepted an agreed work package and is coordinating its delivery. Which process is being applied?
questions.why: Managing product delivery governs the interface between the project manager's authorization and the team's accepted delivery commitments.

questions.stem: The project manager is asked to prepare the next stage plan and refresh the business case. Which process handles this?
questions.why: The stage boundary process prepares the evidence and next-stage planning needed for board authorization.

questions.stem: Users have accepted the final product. What process coordinates handover, lessons and the end project report?
questions.why: Closing a project confirms acceptance, records project performance and provides controlled closure.

questions.stem: A project must stop early because its justification has disappeared. Which process still applies to an authorized premature closure?
options: Managing product delivery must continue to completion
questions.why: PRINCE2 uses a controlled closing process even when the project ends prematurely.

questions.stem: Which process starts before project initiation and is used to prevent unsuitable projects proceeding?
questions.why: Startup gives decision-makers enough information to determine whether initiation is justified.

questions.stem: Which statement about directing a project is correct?
options: Board direction runs from early authorization decisions through project closure
It is performed only inside the initiation stage
It ends as soon as the first stage plan is approved
It is the same as the team manager's daily product delivery
questions.why: The directing process provides ongoing governance over the project lifecycle.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about projects are correct?
1. They are temporary.
2. They are always identical to past projects.
3. They introduce uncertainty.
4. They are the same as ongoing business as usual.
questions.why: PRINCE2 identifies change, temporary nature, uniqueness, cross-functional work and uncertainty as distinguishing project characteristics.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about tailoring PRINCE2 are correct?
1. Terminology can reflect the organization's language.
2. One of the seven principles may be deleted.
3. Controls can be scaled for complexity.
4. Every project needs identical paperwork.
questions.why: Tailoring can adapt terminology, management products and control detail, but does not remove the seven principles.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about people are correct?
1. Stakeholders can include people affected by the project who do not work on it.
2. Leadership only means instructing tasks.
3. Co-creation involves users and influencers in design.
4. Every stakeholder must be on the project board.
questions.why: The people element includes impacted stakeholders; leadership goes beyond management instruction and co-creation improves adoption.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about value are correct?
1. An output is a deliverable.
2. A benefit is a measurable improvement from an outcome.
3. Every outcome is automatically a financial benefit.
4. A dis-benefit is always an uncertain risk.
questions.why: Outputs can enable changed outcomes; those changes can produce measurable benefits and dis-benefits.

questions.stem:
Which TWO role statements are correct?
1. One project executive is ultimately accountable for project success.
2. Senior supplier defines all user benefits.
3. Senior user represents the interests of users and expected benefits.
4. The team manager must always sit on the project board.
questions.why: The executive owns business accountability; the senior user focuses on requirements, adoption and benefits; supplier interests sit with senior supplier.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about plans are correct?
1. A team plan is optional.
2. A project plan is a detailed daily task schedule for every stage.
3. A stage plan is a detailed control baseline for a management stage.
4. An exception plan can never replace a stage plan.
questions.why: A project plan is high level for the whole project; a stage plan is detailed, and an optional team plan may support a work package.

questions.stem:
Which TWO quality statements are correct?
1. Quality assurance is generally independent of the project team.
2. Quality control checks specific products against their requirements.
3. Acceptance criteria only concern time and cost.
4. Requirements cannot be revised under approved change control.
questions.why: Product tests are quality control; systematic independent confidence in the arrangements is quality assurance.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about risks are correct?
1. A threat could harm objectives if it happens.
2. An opportunity could help objectives if it happens.
3. Every risk has already occurred.
4. Every risk action owner must be the executive.
questions.why: A risk is uncertain and may be a threat or an opportunity; owners and action owners can be assigned as appropriate.

questions.stem:
Which TWO issue statements are correct?
1. A request for change proposes an alteration to an approved baseline.
2. Off-specification means a product will not meet its specification.
3. Every issue is merely an uncertain future risk.
4. All issues require a board-approved exception plan.
questions.why: Change requests and off-specifications are issue types; responses and approvals depend on impact and delegated authority.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about progress reports are correct?
1. A checkpoint report can go from team manager to project manager.
2. A highlight report can go from project manager to project board.
3. Exception reports are only made after actual tolerance breaches.
4. An end project report is prepared before starting up.
questions.why: Time-driven checkpoint and highlight reports connect the levels; exceptions are forecast deviations beyond tolerance.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about processes are correct?
1. Directing a project is mainly a project board process.
2. Managing product delivery is run by the project board to authorize stage boundaries.
3. Controlling a stage is mainly a project manager process.
4. Closing a project is performed before initiating a project.
questions.why: Board-level direction is distinct from project manager stage control and team-level product delivery.

questions.stem: Identify the missing words: Risk [?] describes how close in time an uncertain risk event may occur.
questions.why: Proximity refers to how near in time a risk may occur; velocity measures how quickly its effects arise afterward.

questions.stem: Identify the missing words: A forecast deviation beyond an agreed tolerance is an [?].
questions.why: PRINCE2 escalates a forecast exception; it is not necessary to wait for the deviation to happen.

questions.stem: Identify the missing words: The [?] is the single role ultimately accountable for project success and business justification.
questions.why: The executive is appointed by the business and is ultimately accountable for project success.

questions.stem: Identify the missing words: A proposal to modify a project baseline is a request for [?].
questions.why: A request for change is an issue type involving an approved project baseline.

questions.stem: Which action is NOT normally an example of quality control?
options: Independently evaluating the overall quality management system
Testing a finished product against its agreed tolerances
Checking a component meets its specifications
questions.why: Independent systematic evaluation of quality arrangements is quality assurance, while product checks and tests are quality control.

questions.stem: Which is NOT a purpose of closing a project?
options: Authorizing every work package for the next stage
Confirming the project product is accepted
Reviewing performance against the project's baselines
Preparing the end project report and follow-on recommendations
questions.why: Closing confirms acceptance, evaluates delivery and makes an orderly handover rather than starting another delivery stage.

questions.stem: A retailer runs its existing tills every day and separately forms a temporary team to launch a new checkout system. Which activity is a project?
options: Both activities, because they involve staff
The temporary launch team delivering the new system
Neither activity, because retail systems are business operations
questions.why: The team is temporary, cross-functional and has a specific change and product to deliver.
optionWhy: Operations continue indefinitely. A change initiative can be a project but routine tills are not themselves projects.
Till operation is business as usual, with no defined temporary change deliverable.
The team is temporary, cross-functional and has a specific change and product to deliver.
PRINCE2 is not restricted by industry: a retailer can run projects to introduce change.

questions.stem: A construction project completes a fixed building phase, then improves a visitor-booking application in short cycles. Which delivery approach best describes this combination?
questions.why: Hybrid combines different specialist delivery approaches within one project; governance stays in place.
optionWhy: Hybrid combines different specialist delivery approaches within one project; governance stays in place.
The application part is iterative, but it does not describe the fixed construction work.
The building work is sequential, but the application is delivered iteratively.
Using a mix of approved approaches does not remove control or make delivery uncontrolled.

questions.stem: A project proposes faster service but will consume significantly more electricity. Which performance aspect makes the increased energy use directly relevant?
questions.why: Sustainability assesses agreed environmental, social and governance performance targets.
optionWhy: Time relates to delivery dates, not the project’s environmental impact.
Sustainability assesses agreed environmental, social and governance performance targets.
Quality asks whether deliverables meet requirements; energy use may matter separately as sustainability.
Scope describes the agreed products or deliverables, not sustainability impact directly.

questions.stem: A board reviews a new forecast and decides to stop the project because expected value no longer justifies additional cost. Which principle is decisive?
questions.why: The justification must remain desirable, viable and achievable; a project can be stopped when it no longer is.
optionWhy: Learning from experience is about using lessons to improve practice, not the investment decision itself.
Focus on products is about deliverables and their quality, not whether investment remains worthwhile.
The justification must remain desirable, viable and achievable; a project can be stopped when it no longer is.
Manage by exception uses tolerances and escalation, but the reason for stopping here is lost business justification.

questions.stem: A project manager discovers a previous team failed to train users. She changes the current handover plan and shares the result. Which principle is most clearly applied?
questions.why: The team identifies a useful lesson, applies it and shares the improved approach.
optionWhy: Manage by stages is about planning and authorising work in management stages.
The team identifies a useful lesson, applies it and shares the improved approach.
Tailoring adapts PRINCE2 controls to context; this stem specifically centres on learning from previous experience.
Defining roles is about accountability and interests, not applying lessons to improve handover.

questions.stem: A very small project has digital combined records but retains all seven guiding obligations and an agreed approval path. Which statement is correct?
options: It is not PRINCE2 unless each document has its own printed file
PRINCE2 principles may be omitted when cost is low
Only the board can write the management records
This can be valid tailoring if the board approves the proposed approach
questions.why: The formality and detail may be tailored, provided the required principles and control decisions remain.
optionWhy: Information and decisions are required, but a separate printed document is not always necessary.
All seven principles remain mandatory even for a small project.
The project manager normally recommends tailoring and prepares management information; the board approves.
The formality and detail may be tailored, provided the required principles and control decisions remain.

questions.stem: Users receive a new system on time but reject it because their daily process was not redesigned. Which management approach most directly addresses the missing preparation?
questions.why: Change management prepares affected people and business processes to move to target ways of working.
optionWhy: Quality management checks that products satisfy specified requirements; adoption can fail even with a quality product.
Change management prepares affected people and business processes to move to target ways of working.
Risk management addresses uncertain threats and opportunities; the issue here is organisational adoption.
Issue management controls issues and changes to approved baselines, not the broader adoption plan.

questions.stem: A remote project sends weekly updates to executives but never asks front-line users for feedback. What is missing from the people element?
questions.why: The communication approach should allow feedback from people affected and critical to success.
optionWhy: An issue register captures project issues but does not establish two-way engagement.
Quality tolerance relates to measurable product quality, not consultation with stakeholders.
The communication approach should allow feedback from people affected and critical to success.
An exception plan addresses a forecast tolerance breach; none is described.

questions.stem: A project leader brings employees and key influencers into designing the new work process so they will adopt it. What concept best describes this?
questions.why: Co-creation is collaborative design involving users and key influencers to support adoption.
optionWhy: Co-creation is collaborative design involving users and key influencers to support adoption.
Change control handles amendments to an approved baseline, rather than collaborative design itself.
Quality assurance gives confidence in quality methods, usually independently.
Event-driven control occurs when a defined event happens and is not a collaboration model.

questions.stem: A clinic installs electronic check-in kiosks. Waiting time later falls by seven minutes on average. Which item is the benefit?
options: The ability to check in electronically
The measured seven-minute reduction in waiting time
The training materials given to receptionists
questions.why: The measured reduction is an improvement produced by changed behaviour and supports a business objective.
optionWhy: Kiosks are outputs: deliverables of the project.
Electronic check-in is a capability/outcome depending on usage; a measurable advantageous improvement is required for benefit.
The measured reduction is an improvement produced by changed behaviour and supports a business objective.
Training materials are outputs enabling adoption, not themselves a measured improvement.

questions.stem: A digital project should reduce paper use but is expected to increase annual electricity costs. What should the business case do with the increase?
options: Ignore it because the project is environmentally positive overall
Record and assess it as a potential dis-benefit or ongoing cost
Hide it in the stage plan until closing
Treat it automatically as a risk that may never occur
questions.why: A foreseeable ongoing negative consequence or cost needs explicit analysis in the justification.
optionWhy: A positive benefit does not cancel the need to evaluate measurable negative consequences.
A foreseeable ongoing negative consequence or cost needs explicit analysis in the justification.
Plans describe delivery; the case needs to present financial and non-financial impacts to decision makers.
A known expected operational cost is not simply an uncertain risk that may never happen.

questions.stem: A project has closed. Who should use which approach to schedule checks that forecast benefits have actually occurred?
options: Project manager using the issue register
Team manager using a team plan
Relevant business owners using the benefits management approach
questions.why: The benefits management approach sets actions and reviews, and benefits may require business ownership after closure.
optionWhy: An issue register is for issues, not the planned benefits review schedule.
A team plan controls a work package while the project is delivering, not post-project benefits verification.
A product description defines product quality, not how benefits will be reviewed later.
The benefits management approach sets actions and reviews, and benefits may require business ownership after closure.

questions.stem: Before the project board begins governing a new programme portal, who is responsible for setting project-level tolerances?
questions.why: The commissioning business layer establishes project tolerances within which the board directs.
optionWhy: The commissioning business layer establishes project tolerances within which the board directs.
The project manager controls within stage tolerances set by the board.
The senior supplier represents technical and delivery interests, not alone the commissioning limits.
The team manager works within agreed work-package tolerances, not project-level limits.

questions.stem: The project has one person accountable for continued value and investment, but several people represent different user communities. Which statement is correct?
options: There can be multiple executives if there are multiple users
The project manager must also be the executive
There is one executive but potentially multiple senior users
The senior supplier must chair all user meetings
questions.why: There must be one executive; more than one senior user can represent a complex user community.
optionWhy: The PRINCE2 executive role is a single point of accountability even with several user groups.
The executive and project manager roles must not be held by the same person.
There must be one executive; more than one senior user can represent a complex user community.
The senior supplier represents supplier delivery expertise, not user community leadership.

questions.stem: A project support officer is asked to provide independent assurance of the project manager’s work. Why is this problematic?
options: All project support roles must be external suppliers
Independent project assurance must remain separate from project support
Only the project manager can perform project assurance
Project assurance never considers the quality of products
questions.why: Project support provides assistance to day-to-day management, while assurance must examine it independently on behalf of the board.
optionWhy: Project support may be internal, external or delegated; that is not the issue.
Project support provides assistance to day-to-day management, while assurance must examine it independently on behalf of the board.
The board establishes project assurance; it should not depend on the manager whose work is being assured.
Product quality is one of the areas that project assurance may review.

questions.stem: A project manager needs to tell the board how all major project products, costs and dates fit together, before detailing the next stage. Which plan is appropriate?
questions.why: The project plan gives the high-level picture of products, timing and cost across the project.
optionWhy: A team plan is optional work-package detail, not the entire project picture.
A stage plan controls one management stage in greater detail.
The project plan gives the high-level picture of products, timing and cost across the project.
An exception plan replaces an out-of-tolerance plan in response to an exception.

questions.stem: A team is told to estimate programming tasks before anybody agrees what the finished service must do. Which planning principle is at risk?
questions.why: Product-based planning should specify deliverables and quality criteria before estimating work.
optionWhy: Product-based planning should specify deliverables and quality criteria before estimating work.
Managing by stages concerns investment stages and planning horizons, not the starting point for estimating.
Learning from experience may inform estimates, but the problem is undefined products.
Manage by exception addresses delegated limits and escalations, not the product definition sequence.

questions.stem: Stage work is forecast to exceed its cost tolerance. The board requests a realistic replacement for the stage plan. What should the project manager prepare?
questions.why: An exception plan shows how to respond to the forecast breach and may replace the existing stage plan after approval.
optionWhy: The mandate triggers the project at startup, not a replacement stage response.
The work package description defines work delegated to a team, not a replacement stage baseline.
The benefits management approach sets benefits reviews, not delivery replanning after exception.
An exception plan shows how to respond to the forecast breach and may replace the existing stage plan after approval.

questions.stem: A tester measures the response time of a newly built portal against the target in its product description. Which activity is this?
questions.why: Quality control checks the actual product against defined quality specifications.
optionWhy: Quality assurance checks confidence in the project quality system and is typically independent of delivery.
Change management prepares people and business working practices for transition.
Quality control checks the actual product against defined quality specifications.
Project assurance examines project performance independently for the board, not normally this specific test execution.

questions.stem: Users will only accept the finished mobile service if it passes a specified set of prioritised conditions. What are these conditions called?
questions.why: Acceptance criteria define the conditions the overall project product must satisfy for user acceptance.
optionWhy: Acceptance criteria define the conditions the overall project product must satisfy for user acceptance.
Risk tolerance sets measurable bounds for uncertainty, not sign-off conditions.
The quality register records quality activities and results; it does not define overall acceptance terms.
A work breakdown structure decomposes the work, not acceptance conditions.

questions.stem: The project manager wants to know which products have been formally approved and which remain in testing. What record is designed for that overview?
questions.why: The product register records product identity, status and approvals through delivery.
optionWhy: The lessons log tracks project learning, not individual product status.
The product register records product identity, status and approvals through delivery.
The communication approach sets stakeholder information and feedback methods.
An exception report escalates a forecast breach of tolerance.

questions.stem: A possible future supplier strike could delay deployment. It has not happened yet. Which practice should assess its probability and impact?
questions.why: The risk practice identifies and assesses uncertainty, including threats and opportunities.
optionWhy: Issues is concerned with something requiring management consideration now; the strike remains uncertain.
Quality defines requirements and control, not assessing an uncertain external event.
Progress checks actual versus planned delivery and exceptions, but identifying/assessing uncertainty belongs to Risk.
The risk practice identifies and assesses uncertainty, including threats and opportunities.

questions.stem: A risk owner approves the overall response plan and asks a colleague to carry out a supplier contingency test. What is the colleague?
questions.why: A risk action owner is specifically assigned to perform an agreed response action.
optionWhy: The senior user represents user requirements, adoption and benefits, not the assigned response task.
A risk action owner is specifically assigned to perform an agreed response action.
The executive owns business justification and investment accountability, not this delegated contingency task.
Project assurance is independent oversight, not the person directed to carry out the risk response.

questions.stem: A possible positive event could reduce installation costs. The project funds a pilot to make the improvement more likely. What response is that?
questions.why: Enhancement increases the likelihood or positive impact of an opportunity.
optionWhy: Enhancement increases the likelihood or positive impact of an opportunity.
Avoiding a threat removes or prevents a negative uncertain event, not a positive one.
The pilot is an active response, so it is not simply acceptance without action.
Transfer reallocates a threat’s financial effect, rather than increasing a potential benefit.

questions.stem: A sponsor requests a different user interface after the approved product specification was baselined. What type of issue is this?
questions.why: A proposed modification to the approved product baseline is a request for change.
optionWhy: An opportunity is an uncertain favourable event; this is a specific proposal to change an approved baseline.
Quality assurance is independent confidence in standards, not a proposal to change approved specifications.
A proposed modification to the approved product baseline is a request for change.
Risk appetite concerns the willingness to take uncertainty, not this proposal to change a product.

questions.stem: The impact of a logged change request on business case, risks and delivery scope needs to be understood. Which issue technique step is next?
questions.why: Assess examines impact and severity after an issue has been captured.
optionWhy: Assess examines impact and severity after an issue has been captured.
Capture registers and classifies an issue but does not complete its impact assessment.
Implement executes a decision after authorisation; the change has not yet been decided.
Decide chooses an option within delegated authority after assessment and recommendation.

questions.stem: A component is now expected not to achieve an agreed technical specification, even though the team will still deliver it. What is the clearest issue type?
questions.why: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its agreed specification.
optionWhy: The change budget funds approved changes; it is not a type of product failure.
An off-specification is a product that will not meet its agreed specification.
Risk proximity is the timing of a possible uncertain event, not a failure against specification.
Product acceptance is an approval event, not a name for an anticipated specification failure.

questions.stem: The team manager predicts its work package will go over the agreed duration tolerance. Who should normally be informed first?
questions.why: The project manager sets work-package tolerances and receives the team manager’s escalation.
optionWhy: The business layer sets project limits but does not control individual team work-package issues.
The project board governs at stage level; work-package problems are first escalated to the project manager.
The senior user represents user interests and is not the normal work-package control escalation recipient.
The project manager sets work-package tolerances and receives the team manager’s escalation.

questions.stem: The project board requires a brief summary every two weeks about the stage being managed. Which report best supports this?
questions.why: A highlight report is the project manager’s regular summary of stage progress to the board.
optionWhy: A checkpoint report is regular work-package progress from team manager to project manager.
A highlight report is the project manager’s regular summary of stage progress to the board.
An exception report is event-driven escalation of a forecast tolerance breach, not a routine fortnightly summary.
An end project report is prepared for closure and overall performance evaluation.

questions.stem: A forecast shows that stage costs will exceed the tolerance granted by the board. What has occurred in PRINCE2 terms?
questions.why: An exception is a forecast deviation beyond the relevant delegated tolerance.
optionWhy: An exception is a forecast deviation beyond the relevant delegated tolerance.
A risk is uncertainty and may exist even when no plan tolerance has been forecast to be exceeded.
A change is modification to a baseline; a cost forecast breach does not necessarily mean a change has been approved.
Quality approval concerns product requirements, not a stage cost forecast.

questions.stem: The project board must decide whether to invest in detailed initiation. Which process creates the early project brief and initiation stage plan?
questions.why: Starting up a project tests viability cheaply, prepares the project brief and plans initiation.
optionWhy: Initiating a project develops full project foundations and PID after initiation has been authorised.
Closing a project confirms handover and evaluates performance at the end or premature end.
Starting up a project tests viability cheaply, prepares the project brief and plans initiation.
Managing product delivery controls the team’s acceptance, execution and delivery of work packages.

questions.stem: At the end of a management stage, updated business justification and a proposed plan for the next stage are needed. Who prepares these for board consideration?
options: Managing a stage boundary process led by the project manager
Directing a project process led by the team manager
Managing product delivery process led by the senior user
Closing a project process led by project support
questions.why: The project manager uses managing a stage boundary to prepare end stage evidence, updated justification and the next plan.
optionWhy: The project manager uses managing a stage boundary to prepare end stage evidence, updated justification and the next plan.
Directing a project is the board’s oversight; it does not run the team-manager stage-planning work.
Managing product delivery covers executing work packages under the team manager, not planning future stages.
Closing a project is for final/premature closure and does not normally prepare a subsequent stage.

questions.stem: External conditions make continued delivery unjustified and the board orders the project stopped. What should happen to closure?
options: Skip closure because the work was not finished
The team manager issues a new project mandate
The board automatically transfers budget without reviewing products
Use the closing a project process to manage premature closure
questions.why: Closing a project also applies to premature closure to make responsibilities and incomplete work clear.
optionWhy: Premature projects still need orderly recording, handover, risk handling and authorisation.
A project mandate commissions a new project, not closes one.
Budget transfer is a business decision and cannot replace controlled project closure.
Closing a project also applies to premature closure to make responsibilities and incomplete work clear.

questions.stem: A project combines detailed design followed by construction in a fixed sequence, but develops its customer portal in repeated small releases. Which term BEST describes its delivery approach?
questions.why: Hybrid combines delivery approaches in one PRINCE2-governed project.
optionWhy: Business as usual describes continuing operations, not a temporary project delivering change.
Hybrid combines delivery approaches in one PRINCE2-governed project.
Iterative-incremental fits the portal component but does not describe the full mix.
Linear-sequential fits the design-and-build component but not the portal delivered incrementally.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements describe the integrated elements of PRINCE2 Project Management?
1. People includes those working on and affected by the project.
2. Processes replace the need for practices.
3. Project context influences how the method is applied.
4. Practices are optional when a project is small.
questions.why: Both 1 and 3 are true: people and context are among PRINCE2’s five integrated elements.
optionWhy: Statement 3 is true, but 4 is false: the practices may be tailored, not discarded.
Both 2 and 4 are false: processes do not replace practices, and practices must still be addressed with proportionate tailoring.
Both 1 and 3 are true: people and context are among PRINCE2’s five integrated elements.
Statement 1 is true, but 2 is false: processes and practices are integrated, not substitutes.

questions.stem: A team begins defining detailed activities before agreeing which products meet user requirements. Which principle should it apply more carefully?
questions.why: Focus on products means define the deliverables and their quality requirements before planning tasks in detail.
optionWhy: Learn from experience uses lessons, but the immediate weakness is failure to define required products.
Manage by exception defines delegated tolerances; no tolerance breach is described.
Manage by stages sets management decision points, not the order of product-based planning here.
Focus on products means define the deliverables and their quality requirements before planning tasks in detail.

questions.stem: A project manager suggests combining several management products into one digital record. Who is accountable for approving how PRINCE2 is tailored?
questions.why: The project board is accountable for tailoring decisions; the project manager proposes the approach.
optionWhy: The project board is accountable for tailoring decisions; the project manager proposes the approach.
Project support can maintain records but is not accountable for approving tailoring.
The senior supplier represents supplier interests but cannot alone approve how the method is tailored.
The team manager executes work packages and does not govern project-level tailoring.

questions.stem: Identify the missing words: PRINCE2 management by [?] permits decisions within delegated limits unless a forecast exceeds tolerance.
questions.why: Management by exception uses tolerances to delegate decisions and escalate forecast breaches.
optionWhy: Business case gives justification; it does not name the tolerance-based delegation principle.
Management by exception uses tolerances to delegate decisions and escalate forecast breaches.
Management stages provide review points; stage boundary is not the delegation principle.
Product acceptance is a quality/closure decision and not the overall delegation method.

questions.stem: A project team wants to replace PRINCE2 terminology with names already familiar across the organization. What should the project manager do?
options: Create a new principle for the revised terms
Drop the roles that have inconvenient names
Propose terminology changes for board approval and document the tailoring in the PID
Change the names without recording the decision
questions.why: Terminology can be tailored, with project-manager recommendation, board approval and PID documentation.
optionWhy: The seven principles are obligatory and are not renamed or replaced by newly invented principles.
Changing terminology does not remove role responsibilities and business, user and supplier interests.
Terminology can be tailored, with project-manager recommendation, board approval and PID documentation.
Tailoring decisions need to be agreed and documented, rather than changed without control.

questions.stem: A board authorizes only the next manageable portion of work after checking the updated business case. Which principle most directly describes this governance pattern?
questions.why: Manage by stages allows planning and authorization at stage boundaries rather than committing all delivery detail at once.
optionWhy: Defined roles clarify authority, but the staged sequence is the decisive clue.
Focus on products defines deliverables; it does not explain successive authorization points.
Using lessons would support better decisions, but the question describes stage-based controls.
Manage by stages allows planning and authorization at stage boundaries rather than committing all delivery detail at once.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements are consistent with the principle of continued business justification?
1. A project must begin with sufficient reason to invest.
2. A project continues automatically once delivery has started.
3. The justification is checked as circumstances change.
4. A finished output is proof that benefits have been realized.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: the initial reason for investment must remain valid.
optionWhy: 1 and 3 are true: the initial reason for investment must remain valid.
3 is true but 2 is false: a project can be stopped if justification is lost.
Both 2 and 4 are false: neither automatic continuation nor automatic benefits are PRINCE2 principles.
1 is true but 4 is false: outputs do not automatically demonstrate realized benefits.

questions.stem: A new scheduling system works correctly, but service managers refuse to use it. Which activity most directly supports the project’s intended benefits?
options: Issuing an exception plan solely because users have concerns
Planning how staff move to new working practices
Increasing system testing without asking users
questions.why: Change management prepares the transition from current ways of working to the target organizational state.
optionWhy: An exception plan follows an agreed tolerance exception; the need here is to address people and adoption.
Change management prepares the transition from current ways of working to the target organizational state.
Change control can authorize changes; an indefinite freeze prevents adaptation and does not solve adoption.
Further product tests may be useful but do not in themselves address adoption by operating teams.

questions.stem: Two project teams have identical technical skills but achieve different results because trust and relationships differ. Which people concept does this BEST illustrate?
options: Project context is irrelevant when people are qualified
Relationships and team dynamics affect performance
questions.why: PRINCE2 recognises that interactions, culture and relationships influence how effectively a team works.
optionWhy: Reporting controls do not fully explain differences in teamwork or trust.
The project ecosystem and context remain relevant even when individuals are competent.
PRINCE2 recognises that interactions, culture and relationships influence how effectively a team works.
Individual capability matters but does not guarantee equivalent team performance.

questions.stem: Identify the missing term: A person who can influence a project, is affected by it, or perceives an effect is a [?].
questions.why: Stakeholder covers individuals, groups or organizations affecting or affected by the project, including perceived effects.
optionWhy: A team manager is a specific delivery role; many stakeholders have no formal project role.
Project support is a defined service function within the project team.
A risk owner is assigned to manage an identified risk, not the broader stakeholder definition.
Stakeholder covers individuals, groups or organizations affecting or affected by the project, including perceived effects.

questions.stem: A manager assigns tasks, checks that agreed procedures are followed and coordinates delivery. Which term best names this behaviour?
questions.why: Management includes directing execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working.
optionWhy: Management includes directing execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working.
Co-creation brings users and influencers together to design products or ways of working.
Leadership primarily motivates and influences people towards shared objectives.
Cultural intelligence helps people work across cultures; it is not the core definition of managing tasks.

questions.stem: Users and key influencers jointly design the future customer-service process so that it will be adopted. What is this specifically called?
questions.why: Co-creation is collaborative design with users and influencers that supports adoption.
optionWhy: Quality assurance provides independent confidence in quality processes and standards.
Co-creation is collaborative design with users and influencers that supports adoption.
A product register tracks product status; it does not describe collaborative design.
Change control is about assessed changes to a baselined product, not collaborative design itself.

questions.stem: A communication approach schedules messages to stakeholders but has no process for stakeholders to respond. Which improvement best supports PRINCE2 7?
options: Replace it with a one-way progress newsletter
Escalate every comment to the project board
Communicate only when an exception occurs
questions.why: The communication management approach should facilitate controlled, two-way information and feedback.
optionWhy: A newsletter alone remains one-way and misses stakeholder feedback.
Most feedback should be handled at the appropriate delegated level, not automatically by the board.
The communication management approach should facilitate controlled, two-way information and feedback.
Event-driven exception communication is important but does not replace regular engagement.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about the project ecosystem are correct?
1. People affected by the project may sit outside its formal team.
2. All key influencers must be senior executives.
3. Supplier relationships may cross organizational boundaries.
4. Once the team is appointed, stakeholders never change.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: project relationships extend beyond the formal team and may cross organizations.
optionWhy: 3 is true but 2 is false: key influencers can include operational colleagues, not just executives.
2 and 4 are false: influence is not restricted to seniority and stakeholder needs evolve.
1 is true but 4 is false: stakeholders and influence can change throughout the project.
1 and 3 are true: project relationships extend beyond the formal team and may cross organizations.

questions.stem: What is the principal purpose of the communication management approach?
options: Describe stakeholder information needs, channels, frequency and feedback
Specify who is permitted to approve changes to product baselines
Define the quality criteria for accepting the project product
Record all identified risk owners and their responses
questions.why: Communication management defines how information is exchanged and feedback obtained across the project ecosystem.
optionWhy: Communication management defines how information is exchanged and feedback obtained across the project ecosystem.
The issue management approach and change authority cover changes to baselines.
The project product description and quality approach cover acceptance and specifications.
The risk register and risk management approach deal with risk information and assignments.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes change management from change control in PRINCE2 7?
options: Change control manages staff training; change management logs defects
Change management prepares adoption of new ways of working; change control governs amendments to approved baselines
Both exclusively authorize revisions to baselined products
Neither term concerns users outside the project team
questions.why: The distinction is people adopting target-state working practices versus assessing and authorizing baseline changes.
optionWhy: Training may support change management, while defects and requests for change belong in issue management.
The distinction is people adopting target-state working practices versus assessing and authorizing baseline changes.
Change management concerns organizational transition; change control is a different function within issue management.
Users and other stakeholders affected by the change are vital to both decisions and adoption.

questions.stem: When developing a diverse hybrid team, which action is most consistent with the people guidance?
options: Use the same informal communication routine for everyone regardless of location
Assume identical abilities because job titles match
Identify capability gaps and build trust across locations and cultures
questions.why: Effective teams assess capabilities, diversity, cultural intelligence and ways to build cohesion.
optionWhy: Communication should be tailored to co-located, remote and hybrid working arrangements.
People with the same title can have different competencies and needs.
Effective teams assess capabilities, diversity, cultural intelligence and ways to build cohesion.
Supplier participants may be essential members of the project ecosystem and collaboration.

questions.stem: A council delivers new waste-sorting bins. Six months later, the percentage of material recycled rises measurably. Which item is the benefit?
questions.why: The measurable improvement perceived as valuable is a benefit.
optionWhy: The bins are project outputs: tangible deliverables of the activity.
An ability to separate waste is capability; its use may lead to an outcome.
The installation timetable is planning information, not a business benefit.
The measurable improvement perceived as valuable is a benefit.

questions.stem: The project manager updates forecast costs and risks in the business case after a supplier changes its price. Which business case technique step is most directly being performed?
questions.why: Maintain keeps the business case current as costs, risks and forecasts change.
optionWhy: Maintain keeps the business case current as costs, risks and forecasts change.
Confirm considers actual or expected realization of benefits, often after delivery.
Develop establishes and elaborates the case initially, including evaluating options.
Accept is not one of the four named business case management technique steps.

questions.stem: At an end-stage decision the board asks whether the project remains desirable, viable and achievable. Which step of business case management is being applied?
questions.why: Check assesses whether the business justification remains sound at decision points.
optionWhy: Capture is an issues technique activity, not the business case check step.
Check assesses whether the business justification remains sound at decision points.
Confirm addresses whether expected benefits were or will be realized.
Implement belongs to risk or issue response work, not a named business case step.

questions.stem: Identify the missing word: A measurable adverse effect resulting from an outcome, perceived as negative by the investing organization, is a [?].
questions.why: A dis-benefit is a measurable decline stemming from an outcome, not merely a possible future event.
optionWhy: A product is an output, not a measured negative effect.
A request for change proposes modifying a controlled baseline.
A dis-benefit is a measurable decline stemming from an outcome, not merely a possible future event.
A risk is uncertain; a dis-benefit is the measurable negative consequence of an outcome.

questions.stem: A project delivers its main product successfully, but realization of savings will take two years. What should happen to the scheduled benefits reviews?
options: The team manager keeps the project open indefinitely
The benefits are recorded as already achieved at handover
They cease as soon as the project closes
They continue in accordance with the benefits management approach under suitable business ownership
questions.why: The benefits management approach supports post-project reviews and assigned accountability for realization.
optionWhy: Keeping a temporary project alive for years is not necessary solely to conduct benefits reviews.
Outputs being handed over does not prove future measurable savings have happened.
Project closure does not mean all planned benefits reviews are cancelled.
The benefits management approach supports post-project reviews and assigned accountability for realization.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about establishing business justification are correct?
1. The do-nothing option helps form an investment comparison.
2. All expected benefits must occur before a project can close.
3. Associated risks and dis-benefits can affect the choice.
4. The business case is unnecessary after initiation.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: investment options must be compared considering risks and adverse effects.
optionWhy: 1 and 3 are true: investment options must be compared considering risks and adverse effects.
Both 2 and 4 are false: benefit realization may follow closure and the business case stays under review.
1 is true but 2 false: benefits can be realized after project closure.
3 is true but 4 false: continued justification requires a live business case.

questions.stem: An organization wants the project to minimize its carbon footprint and sets measurable targets and review controls. Which management approach covers the actions for these targets?
questions.why: Sustainability management approach defines actions, reviews and controls for achieving sustainability targets.
optionWhy: Communication approach governs stakeholder information exchange, not the sustainability controls themselves.
Sustainability management approach defines actions, reviews and controls for achieving sustainability targets.
Commercial management covers procurement and commercial relationships, not specifically target reviews for sustainability.
An issue report assesses a particular issue, not the ongoing sustainability management strategy.

questions.stem: The project board wants one individual ultimately accountable for the project’s business justification and funding. Which role is this?
questions.why: The project executive is the single point of accountability for the investment and continuing business case.
optionWhy: The project manager runs the project day to day within authority but is not the overall business-accountable executive.
Senior user represents adoption, requirements and benefits but is not the single overall accountable business lead.
The project executive is the single point of accountability for the investment and continuing business case.
Senior supplier represents the supplier perspective and technical integrity.

questions.stem: The executive is asked to appoint the same individual as the project manager because the project is small. What should happen?
options: Remove the executive if there is a project board
Give all accountability to project support
Combine both roles automatically because the project is small
Keep the project executive and project manager roles separate
questions.why: PRINCE2 does not allow the single accountable executive to be combined with the day-to-day project manager.
optionWhy: The executive is a key member and chair of the board; the role cannot be removed.
Project support is a service role, not the project’s single business-accountable executive.
The two roles cannot be combined; size does not override this separation.
PRINCE2 does not allow the single accountable executive to be combined with the day-to-day project manager.

questions.stem: A team manager is asked to deliver a work package within cost and time constraints. Who normally defines those work-package tolerances?
questions.why: The project manager delegates work packages to teams and sets their tolerances.
optionWhy: The project manager delegates work packages to teams and sets their tolerances.
The senior user represents requirements and benefits, not the normal delegation of team tolerances.
The board sets stage-level tolerances for the project manager, rather than individual work-package limits.
The business layer sets project-level tolerances.

questions.stem: Which organizational level is OUTSIDE the project management team?
questions.why: The business or commissioning layer sits above and outside the project management team.
optionWhy: Managing includes the project manager within the project management team.
The business or commissioning layer sits above and outside the project management team.
Delivering includes team managers and members within the project management structure.
Directing is the project board level within the project management team.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about project assurance are correct?
1. The board is accountable for ensuring its interests are assured.
2. Project assurance should always be performed by the project manager personally.
3. Assurance can be delegated to suitable people with sufficient independence.
4. Project support and assurance must be combined in one person.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: the board retains assurance accountability and may arrange independent assurance.
optionWhy: 1 is true but 4 is false: combining support with assurance compromises independence.
3 is true but 2 is false: the project manager’s own work should not be independently assured by the same person.
1 and 3 are true: the board retains assurance accountability and may arrange independent assurance.
2 and 4 are false: assurance needs independence from day-to-day work and project support.

questions.stem: A work breakdown structure is used in the organization practice. What does it represent?
options: The levels of tolerance delegated by the board
Only the sequence of management stages
A register of known project issues
A hierarchy of the work required for the project
questions.why: The WBS is a hierarchical representation of all the work to be done, linking products to work packages.
optionWhy: Delegated tolerances are management controls, not the purpose of the WBS.
Stage sequencing is part of the plan, not the function of the WBS.
An issue register records issues; it is not a hierarchy of activities.
The WBS is a hierarchical representation of all the work to be done, linking products to work packages.

questions.stem: In organizational design and development, a completed product is handed over to the business team that will operate it. Which step is most directly involved?
options: Transition the project into organizational ecosystem
questions.why: Transition ensures responsibilities and ways of working move into the operational ecosystem.
optionWhy: Transition ensures responsibilities and ways of working move into the operational ecosystem.
Design the ecosystem defines project relationships and accountabilities before transition.
Understand the organization explores existing context and affected groups.
Risk identification is a separate practice activity, not the named handover step.

questions.stem: A supplier needs to know precisely what products to deliver, their quality requirements, constraints and reporting duties. Which management product should be agreed?
questions.why: A work package description records the agreement and constraints for team delivery.
optionWhy: A highlight report summarizes stage progress to the board.
A work package description records the agreement and constraints for team delivery.
The project brief is an early foundation for initiation, not the team’s detailed delivery agreement.
Benefits management describes reviews of outcomes and measurable benefits.

questions.stem: The project manager can accurately estimate the next six weeks but not the detailed work eighteen months away. What planning principle is most applicable?
options: Do not produce a high-level project plan
Delay defining all project products until the final stage
Use a planning horizon with detailed near-term stage plans
Plan the entire project at identical detail now
questions.why: The planning horizon uses detail appropriate to how far ahead the plan reaches, refining later stages nearer their start.
optionWhy: A high-level project plan remains necessary for overall direction and justification.
Major products should be identified at project level, even when later work estimates remain high-level.
The planning horizon uses detail appropriate to how far ahead the plan reaches, refining later stages nearer their start.
Distant detail tends to be less reliable and unnecessary; PRINCE2 supports progressive elaboration.

questions.stem: Identify the missing words: A plan created in response to an exception to replace an existing plan is an [?].
questions.why: An exception plan proposes revised work and control after a tolerance exception, subject to authorization.
optionWhy: An issue report assesses and recommends action for an issue; it is not the replacement plan itself.
A project brief supports early initiation decisions rather than replacing a breached plan.
A team plan is an optional planning level for a work package, not specifically a response to exception.
An exception plan proposes revised work and control after a tolerance exception, subject to authorization.

questions.stem: While constructing a product breakdown structure, the team realizes two products require a supplied component that the project itself will not create. How should this inform planning?
options: Recognize the external dependency and include it in planning assumptions and controls
Treat the product as automatically accepted
Ignore the external product because it is not created by the team
questions.why: External dependencies influence estimates, delivery sequence and required control arrangements.
optionWhy: External dependencies influence estimates, delivery sequence and required control arrangements.
The existence of a supplied product does not prove it meets acceptance or quality requirements.
Identifying a dependency does not establish a realized benefit.
Outside deliverables can still be dependencies that must be monitored.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about PRINCE2 plans are correct?
1. A project plan gives the overall view of the main products.
2. A team plan is mandatory for every work package.
3. A stage plan supports detailed control by the project manager.
4. Every exception plan must replace the entire business case.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: the project plan is high-level and the stage plan is detailed.
optionWhy: Both 2 and 4 are false: team plans are optional and exception plans replace affected plans, not business justification.
1 and 3 are true: the project plan is high-level and the stage plan is detailed.
1 is true but 2 false: team plans are optional, based on need.
3 is true but 4 false: an exception plan is not a replacement business case.

questions.stem: An activity cannot begin until a specialist item arrives from outside the project. What kind of dependency is this?
questions.why: An external dependency relies on something outside the project’s direct control.
optionWhy: A dis-benefit is a measurable adverse outcome, not scheduling dependency.
Tolerance is permitted deviation, not a dependency between activities.
An external dependency relies on something outside the project’s direct control.
An internal dependency is between activities or products managed inside the project.

questions.stem: Who normally uses a stage plan as the primary basis for managing a stage day to day?
questions.why: The project manager uses the stage plan to coordinate and control stage work.
optionWhy: Team manager principally manages work packages; a team plan may be used.
The business layer sets project-wide requirements and tolerances, rather than day-to-day stage work.
The senior supplier assures supplier interests, not overall daily stage coordination.
The project manager uses the stage plan to coordinate and control stage work.

questions.stem: Users will only accept the completed booking system if at least 95% of trial appointments can be booked without errors. What type of information is this?
questions.why: An acceptance criterion defines a condition the overall project product must meet for user acceptance.
optionWhy: An acceptance criterion defines a condition the overall project product must meet for user acceptance.
Risk appetite describes willingness to take uncertainty, not the quality criterion for accepting a system.
Quality assurance gives confidence in the quality system, not the specific threshold for user acceptance.
Issue priority ranks a management problem; the threshold is a product acceptance condition.

questions.stem: An independent department reviews whether the project’s testing procedures comply with organizational standards, rather than testing the finished product. What function is illustrated?
questions.why: Quality assurance gives planned independent confidence in the arrangements that enable product quality.
optionWhy: Quality control performs tests and checks on products and their delivery activities.
Quality assurance gives planned independent confidence in the arrangements that enable product quality.
Product acceptance concerns agreed user sign-off conditions, not an independent methods audit.
Change control governs modifications to approved baselines, not independent quality audits.

questions.stem: The project manager wants to find all planned and completed inspections and their results. Which record is most directly useful?
questions.why: The quality register records quality activities, their schedules and results.
optionWhy: The sustainability approach defines sustainability actions and reviews, not the quality checks register.
The product breakdown structure shows product hierarchy rather than detailed inspection records.
The quality register records quality activities, their schedules and results.
The issue register tracks events requiring management action, not the full planned inspection schedule.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about quality are correct?
1. Quality assurance is typically managed independently of the project team.
2. A completed test automatically means the project product has been accepted.
3. Quality specifications state product measures and target levels.
4. User quality expectations should never be documented.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: assurance is usually independent and specifications define measurable standards.
optionWhy: 3 is true but 4 false: user expectations should be documented in the project product description.
Both 2 and 4 are false: acceptance follows agreed criteria, and expectations must be captured.
1 is true but 2 false: a completed test is evidence, not automatic product acceptance.
1 and 3 are true: assurance is usually independent and specifications define measurable standards.

questions.stem: A project needs to specify the methods, standards and responsibilities for performing quality checks. Which management product should be consulted?
questions.why: The quality management approach explains quality techniques, standards, methods and responsibilities.
optionWhy: The quality management approach explains quality techniques, standards, methods and responsibilities.
The mandate triggers start-up and does not define detailed quality arrangements.
A highlight report summarizes stage status at intervals for the project board.
A risk register records threats and opportunities, not the established quality procedure.

questions.stem: Identify the missing phrase: The prioritized conditions that the overall project product must satisfy before the user accepts it are called [?].
questions.why: Acceptance criteria are the conditions for acceptance of the project product as a whole.
optionWhy: Work-package tolerances are delivery limits delegated to a team.
Acceptance criteria are the conditions for acceptance of the project product as a whole.
Risk responses reduce, exploit or otherwise handle uncertainty.
Project risks are uncertain events affecting objectives, not the user sign-off requirements.

questions.stem: A storm could prevent construction next month. A storm did not occur yet. How should this normally be treated?
questions.why: A risk is an uncertain future event whose occurrence would affect objectives.
optionWhy: An issue describes an event or problem already needing management action; the storm is still uncertain.
An exception is a forecast beyond agreed tolerances; uncertainty alone does not prove one.
A risk is an uncertain future event whose occurrence would affect objectives.
A change modifies an approved baseline; no change has yet been proposed or authorized.

questions.stem: A possible new permit delay is likely to occur soon but would cause little disruption after occurrence. Which concepts distinguish these two assessments?
questions.why: Proximity concerns how soon the event could occur; impact concerns the consequence for objectives.
optionWhy: Ownership concerns assigned responsibilities and stages are management divisions.
Risk appetite describes willingness to accept risk and change budget funds authorized changes.
Velocity concerns speed of effect after occurrence, not the size of the disruption stated.
Proximity concerns how soon the event could occur; impact concerns the consequence for objectives.

questions.stem: The business is willing to take very little uncertainty, and a proposed plan would exceed the defined acceptable exposure threshold. Which two terms distinguish the attitude from the measurable limit?
options: Risk action owner and risk budget
questions.why: Appetite is willingness to take risk; tolerance is the measurable boundary for an objective at risk.
optionWhy: Appetite is willingness to take risk; tolerance is the measurable boundary for an objective at risk.
Outputs and outcomes describe deliverables and the changes they enable.
The action owner and risk budget concern assigned response work and its funding, not willingness and limits.
Velocity and proximity describe speed of impact and nearness of occurrence.

questions.stem: A team is overconfident and ignores the possibility of failure because similar work usually goes well. Which decision-making problem is illustrated?
questions.why: Optimism bias underestimates problems and overestimates the chance of favourable results.
optionWhy: Risk transfer reallocates an aspect of financial exposure to another party, not a thinking bias.
