Optimism bias underestimates problems and overestimates the chance of favourable results.
Loss aversion gives more weight to avoiding losses than gaining equivalent benefits; this example is confidence in success.
Risk tolerance is a measurable limit for an objective at risk, not a cognitive bias.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about risk response are correct?
1. Exploit is appropriate for some opportunities.
2. Avoid is the normal label for maximizing a positive opportunity.
3. Enhance may improve likelihood or impact of an opportunity.
4. All threats must be transferred to an insurer.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: exploit and enhance are opportunity responses.
optionWhy: Both 2 and 4 are false: opportunities may be exploited; threats have several response options.
1 is true but 2 false: avoid is a threat response, whereas exploit concerns opportunities.
1 and 3 are true: exploit and enhance are opportunity responses.
3 is true but 4 false: threats may be reduced, avoided, shared, transferred, accepted or managed contingently.

questions.stem: During risk management, which activity should occur throughout the Identify–Assess–Plan–Implement technique?
options: Authorize every individual response at board level
questions.why: Communication is carried out throughout risk management so relevant stakeholders understand threats and opportunities.
optionWhy: Closure is a separate process, not an activity continuous within every risk technique step.
Risk responses should be authorized at the appropriate delegated level, not automatically by the board.
Project brief development occurs in start-up, not throughout all risk management stages.
Communication is carried out throughout risk management so relevant stakeholders understand threats and opportunities.

questions.stem: The project manager receives a request to revise an already approved product specification. Which issue type applies?
questions.why: A request for change is a proposal to modify the existing approved project baseline.
optionWhy: A request for change is a proposal to modify the existing approved project baseline.
Work-package tolerance is an agreed delivery limit, not an issue category.
Risk proximity measures how soon an uncertain event might occur.
A business opportunity is an unanticipated positive issue, not every requested amendment.

questions.stem: A component will be delivered but will not meet its agreed weight limit. Which issue category fits?
questions.why: Off-specification describes a product that will not meet its agreed specifications.
optionWhy: Outcome describes change resulting from the use of outputs, not a product defect.
Off-specification describes a product that will not meet its agreed specifications.
Quality assurance provides process confidence; it is not the classification of a specific nonconforming product.
Risk appetite is the business’s willingness to take risk, not a product nonconformance.

questions.stem: The project manager evaluates how an issue could change cost, scope, benefits and the risk profile. Which issue-management step does that?
questions.why: Assess investigates consequences and checks severity before recommendations or decisions.
optionWhy: Decide selects a response within delegated authority after an assessment and recommendation.
Implement follows authorization and puts corrective action into effect.
Assess investigates consequences and checks severity before recommendations or decisions.
Capture logs and categorizes the issue so it can be managed.

questions.stem: A change has been approved. The project manager arranges the corrective work and updates the relevant baseline and issue records. Which issue-management step is now being performed?
questions.why: Implement carries out the authorised action and updates records and controlled products as needed.
optionWhy: Assess considers the implications before a recommendation and decision are made.
Capture identifies the issue category and enters it in the register.
Decide is when the authorised person approves or rejects a response; that decision is already complete.
Implement carries out the authorised action and updates records and controlled products as needed.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about project baselines are correct?
1. A baseline contains approved versions of relevant management and project products.
2. Any team member can change a baseline without authorization.
3. Changes to a baseline need the agreed control procedure.
4. Baselines become irrelevant as soon as an issue is raised.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: baselines identify approved versions controlled through change procedures.
optionWhy: 1 and 3 are true: baselines identify approved versions controlled through change procedures.
Both 2 and 4 are false: baselines remain controlled and are the basis for assessing issues.
3 is true but 4 false: the baseline remains the approved reference until changed.
1 is true but 2 false: changes require appropriate authority.

questions.stem: The project board grants a delegated change authority permission to approve changes within an agreed limit. What is the main intended benefit?
options: Decisions can be made at an appropriate level without unnecessary escalation
All future changes become automatically approved
The board is no longer accountable for project performance
questions.why: Delegated authority supports timely decisions within limits while escalation remains available.
optionWhy: Approved changes still need to respect authorized constraints and quality.
Delegated authority supports timely decisions within limits while escalation remains available.
Delegation does not mean proposals are approved without assessment.
The board remains accountable for governance even when some decisions are delegated.

questions.stem: The project manager must define how project information will be stored, secured, processed and used in reporting. Which PID component covers this?
questions.why: The digital and data management approach explains how digital tools and data will be governed and used on the project.
optionWhy: A product description defines an individual deliverable and its quality requirements, not project-wide data governance.
Benefits management defines reviews and actions for realization of outcomes and benefits.
The digital and data management approach explains how digital tools and data will be governed and used on the project.
Change management prepares people to adopt future ways of working, not project data governance.

questions.stem: Actual progress data show a growing pattern of missed milestones even though the current stage is inside tolerance. What is the best use of the information?
options: Focus only on historic reporting because no limit is breached yet
Immediately issue an exception plan without any forecast breach
Stop collecting data until the stage boundary
Use the trend to forecast future stage performance and consider corrective action
questions.why: Trend information helps forecast whether future limits may be exceeded, enabling timely response.
optionWhy: Progress management is forward-looking, not only a report of what has happened.
Exception planning normally follows a forecast exception and appropriate direction; the stem describes a warning trend only.
Waiting would remove the opportunity to make corrections while there is still delegated room to act.
Trend information helps forecast whether future limits may be exceeded, enabling timely response.

questions.stem: A team is slightly behind schedule but still forecasts completing within the agreed work-package tolerance. How should this normally be handled?
options: The team manager should manage the variance within authority and keep the project manager informed
Immediately escalate a stage exception to the board
Stop the project because the baseline cannot change
questions.why: Management by exception permits local corrective action within tolerances, with routine reporting to the project manager.
optionWhy: Management by exception permits local corrective action within tolerances, with routine reporting to the project manager.
A work-package variance does not of itself authorize replacement of the project plan.
A small variance inside work-package tolerance does not automatically become a stage exception.
A variance can be managed; automatic closure would ignore delegated authority and the approved justification.

questions.stem: Identify the missing words: The management product that consolidates significant learning to share with future projects is the [?].
questions.why: A lessons report captures conclusions and recommendations for others to use; it is distinct from the continuing log.
optionWhy: The lessons log collects lessons during the current project; the report summarizes learning for future use.
A lessons report captures conclusions and recommendations for others to use; it is distinct from the continuing log.
A checkpoint report communicates work-package progress to the project manager.
The quality register records quality activities and results, not overarching lessons.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about tolerances are correct?
1. The business layer normally sets project-level tolerances.
2. The project manager sets the project board’s stage-level tolerances.
3. The project board delegates stage tolerances to the project manager.
4. Every small variance automatically requires an exception report.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: project tolerances come from the commissioning level and stage tolerances from the board.
optionWhy: 1 is true but 2 false: the project board, not the project manager, sets stage tolerances.
3 is true but 4 false: exception reports apply when a forecast crosses tolerance.
1 and 3 are true: project tolerances come from the commissioning level and stage tolerances from the board.
2 and 4 are false: board sets stage tolerances and small variances inside tolerance can be managed locally.

questions.stem: The board wants a report comparing overall project achievements against the original project baseline as part of closure. Which report is most appropriate?
questions.why: The end project report compares project results with the original objectives and baselines to support closure.
optionWhy: Issue reports explain individual issues and recommendations, not overall project outcomes.
Highlight reports describe ongoing stage progress at intervals, not final performance against project baseline.
Checkpoint reports detail work-package progress from delivery to project management.
The end project report compares project results with the original objectives and baselines to support closure.

questions.stem: A project mandate has arrived, but the board wants to know if investing in detailed initiation is worthwhile. Which process should occur first?
questions.why: Starting up a project checks whether there is a viable proposal before spending significant effort on initiation.
optionWhy: Starting up a project checks whether there is a viable proposal before spending significant effort on initiation.
Initiating a project establishes detailed foundations after the initiation stage has been authorized.
Closing a project handles completion or premature termination, not initial commissioning.
Controlling a stage coordinates authorized stage work and is not the initial viability check.

questions.stem: A proposed project has only a mandate and an outline business case. Before the board authorizes full delivery, what additional foundation is normally required?
options: The detailed project initiation documentation prepared during initiating a project
An issue report closing every possible uncertainty
questions.why: The PID and detailed business case provide the sound baseline and approaches for a delivery investment decision.
optionWhy: An end project report is written for closure, not initial authorization.
The PID and detailed business case provide the sound baseline and approaches for a delivery investment decision.
Benefits may arise later; benefits review does not substitute for preparation of the PID.
Not every future uncertainty can be closed; risks are managed, not eliminated by an issue report.

questions.stem: The project manager needs to prepare a detailed business case, project management approaches and the project initiation documentation. Which process is responsible?
questions.why: Initiating a project establishes the robust foundations and PID needed before authorizing delivery.
optionWhy: Managing a stage boundary updates stage evidence and prepares the next stage or an exception plan.
Managing product delivery manages team delivery agreements, not production of the PID.
Initiating a project establishes the robust foundations and PID needed before authorizing delivery.
Starting up produces early information such as the project brief and initiation stage plan.

questions.stem: During the initiation stage of a complex project, the project manager must coordinate work packages, track issues and report progress. Which process provides that day-to-day control?
questions.why: Controlling a stage can apply to the initiation stage and coordinates day-to-day progress and work.
optionWhy: Directing a project covers board-level authorization and direction, not day-to-day project management.
Closing a project is for orderly finish, not operational stage control.
Starting up a project is preliminary decision preparation before initiating.
Controlling a stage can apply to the initiation stage and coordinates day-to-day progress and work.

questions.stem: A team agrees its work package, produces the requested products and hands them back for acceptance. Which process governs this team-level cycle?
questions.why: Managing product delivery governs accepting, executing and delivering work packages.
optionWhy: Managing product delivery governs accepting, executing and delivering work packages.
Managing a stage boundary prepares evidence and next-stage plans for the board.
Directing a project is the board’s authorization and oversight process.
Initiating a project develops the PID and plans, not delivery of every specialist work package.

questions.stem: An end stage report and next stage plan are being prepared to support the board’s continuation decision. Which process produces these?
questions.why: Managing a stage boundary prepares end-stage evidence, updates justification and proposes the next stage plan.
optionWhy: Managing product delivery ensures specialist teams deliver their assigned products.
Managing a stage boundary prepares end-stage evidence, updates justification and proposes the next stage plan.
Controlling a stage manages ongoing stage activity, not the formal end-stage planning package.
Starting up a project provides early project foundations before initiation authorization.

questions.stem: A project is completing its final management stage. The users accept the products, but some follow-on operational action remains. What should the closing process do?
options: Keep the project permanently open until all possible operational improvements occur
Document follow-on action recommendations and arrange an orderly transfer to the appropriate owners
Skip the end project report because outstanding actions exist
questions.why: Closing a project records unresolved matters and follow-on action recommendations while formal acceptance and handover are completed.
optionWhy: Routine ongoing operational responsibilities belong outside the temporary project once properly handed over.
Benefits reviews may continue after closure according to the benefits management approach.
Closing a project records unresolved matters and follow-on action recommendations while formal acceptance and handover are completed.
The end project report is useful especially when there are outstanding matters to record and evaluate.

questions.stem: The project board is reviewing a proposed next stage plan. In which process does the board make its authorization decision?
questions.why: Directing a project contains the board’s decision to authorize a stage or provide direction.
optionWhy: Controlling a stage is day-to-day project-manager control within the authorized stage.
Managing product delivery is performed by the team delivering a work package.
Managing a stage boundary prepares the evidence and next-stage plan for the decision.
Directing a project contains the board’s decision to authorize a stage or provide direction.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements about project processes are correct?
1. The board authorizes initiation through directing a project.
2. Managing product delivery is exclusively a project board process.
3. Closing a project includes confirming product acceptance and handover.
4. Starting up a project is used after completing all delivery stages.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: the board directs authorization and closing checks acceptance and handover.
optionWhy: 1 and 3 are true: the board directs authorization and closing checks acceptance and handover.
3 is true but 4 false: starting up takes place before the project is initiated.
1 is true but 2 false: delivery teams execute managing product delivery.
Both 2 and 4 are false: team delivery is not a board function and start-up precedes initiation.

questions.stem: An exception is forecast during the final management stage. Can managing a stage boundary still be used to prepare an exception plan?
options: No, it is never used during the final stage
Yes, exception planning can be needed at any point, including the final stage
Only if the project is creating its initial project brief
No, all final-stage exceptions are automatically approved
questions.why: PRINCE2 notes that managing a stage boundary may be used to prepare an exception plan even in the final stage.
optionWhy: The normal stage-boundary review is not repeated after the final stage, but exception planning remains possible.
PRINCE2 notes that managing a stage boundary may be used to prepare an exception plan even in the final stage.
Project briefs are prepared in start-up, not for final-stage exception planning.
Exceptions require handling and authorization; they are not automatically accepted.

questions.stem: Which process has the objective of ensuring that the project board can judge performance against agreed objectives and authorize its closure?
questions.why: Closing a project confirms acceptance and handover, evaluates performance, and obtains closure authorization.
optionWhy: Managing product delivery delivers individual work packages rather than closeout of the whole project.
Controlling a stage manages ongoing work and reports during stages.
Closing a project confirms acceptance and handover, evaluates performance, and obtains closure authorization.
Starting up a project assesses whether initiating the project is worthwhile.

questions.stem: The project manager is told a stage tolerance will be exceeded and asked to prepare a replacement plan. Which process prepares the exception plan for board consideration?
questions.why: Managing a stage boundary also prepares exception plans when directed after a tolerance breach.
optionWhy: Starting up is for pre-project viability, not exceptions in an authorized stage.
Closing a project applies when the project is to end, not when delivery will continue under a revised plan.
Managing product delivery executes agreed work packages, not stage-level replacement plans for the board.
Managing a stage boundary also prepares exception plans when directed after a tolerance breach.

questions.stem: A project manager consults five parts of PRINCE2: principles, people, practices, processes, and one more element. What is missing?
questions.why: Project context is the fifth integrated element and affects how PRINCE2 is applied.
optionWhy: Project context is the fifth integrated element and affects how PRINCE2 is applied.
The project board is a governance role within the organizing practice.
The risk register is one management record within the method, not one of its five integrated elements.
A schedule is part of project planning information, not a fifth integrated element.

questions.stem: A supplier joins a project and the team clarifies obligations, authority, reporting and relationships with users. Which principle is MOST directly involved?
questions.why: This principle establishes a structure that engages business, user and supplier interests and clarifies relationships.
optionWhy: Stages support project authorization but do not directly explain the supplier relationship agreements.
This principle establishes a structure that engages business, user and supplier interests and clarifies relationships.
Focus on products is about definitions and quality requirements of deliverables.
Business justification concerns the continuing value of investment, not primarily assigning supplier authority.

questions.stem: The project manager finds that a previous project’s lessons log mentions difficult supplier handovers. What action best applies the associated principle?
options: Read the log only at the end of this project
Give all supplier decisions to the board
Adapt the current handover approach, record what works, and share the learning
Store the log but leave current plans unchanged
questions.why: Learn from experience means seeking, applying and sharing lessons throughout delivery.
optionWhy: Lessons should inform early and ongoing work, not only closure.
Board escalation depends on authority and tolerances, not the existence of a lesson.
Learn from experience means seeking, applying and sharing lessons throughout delivery.
Merely filing lessons is insufficient; they should be actively applied.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST explains the relationship between the organizational ecosystem and the project ecosystem?
options: The organizational ecosystem contains only external suppliers
The project ecosystem includes only people formally paid by the project
The ecosystems must be completely separate to preserve governance
The project ecosystem interacts with the wider organizational ecosystem, including affected groups outside the formal team
questions.why: Projects sit within wider organizations and interact with people who deliver, use and are affected by the work.
optionWhy: The organizational ecosystem includes far more than suppliers, including business and users.
People affected by the project may influence it even without formal appointments.
Healthy project relationships often cross boundaries; isolation is not a PRINCE2 requirement.
Projects sit within wider organizations and interact with people who deliver, use and are affected by the work.

questions.stem: A team member has the competence to complete a task but lacks access to the necessary specialist software. Which consideration should the project manager address?
options: Capability and practical resources needed to perform the role
The business case step called confirm
questions.why: Effective management considers capability, competence and whether assigned people can undertake the work.
optionWhy: Effective management considers capability, competence and whether assigned people can undertake the work.
Stakeholder replacement does not solve missing tools.
Confirm reviews benefits realization and is not a resource availability action.
Motivation alone does not provide access to needed tools or resources.

questions.stem: A project manager persuades different departments to support a difficult change by explaining the common objective and listening to concerns. This is an example of what?
questions.why: Leadership motivates and influences stakeholders in pursuit of project objectives.
optionWhy: Change budget covers authorized baseline changes, not motivating users.
Leadership motivates and influences stakeholders in pursuit of project objectives.
Stage plan baselining is a control activity, not the people behaviour described.
Quality control checks products against agreed requirements, not stakeholder motivation.

questions.stem: What should a project change management approach describe?
options: The money authorized for unplanned baseline changes
A list of product quality test failures
How the organization will progress from its current state to the desired future state
Only the names of suppliers requesting changes
questions.why: Change management supports organizational transition, adoption and the target state needed for objectives.
optionWhy: The change budget and issue management approach relate to controlled modifications to a baseline.
Product test failures are tracked through quality and issue records.
Change management supports organizational transition, adoption and the target state needed for objectives.
Supplier names alone do not explain the people and operating transitions.

questions.stem:
Which TWO approaches help a hybrid project team maintain effective relationships?
1. Agree channels suited to remote and in-person participation.
2. Share information only with formally appointed team members.
3. Seek feedback from users affected by the change.
4. Assume all cultures prefer identical ways of collaborating.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are correct: communication should fit hybrid work and include affected stakeholders.
optionWhy: 2 and 4 are false: projects cross formal and cultural boundaries.
1 is correct but 2 false: stakeholders outside the team also need communication.
3 is correct but 4 false: cultural awareness matters when creating effective teams.
1 and 3 are correct: communication should fit hybrid work and include affected stakeholders.

questions.stem: Which item normally provides the initial firm foundation on which the board decides whether to authorize project initiation?
options: Project brief with an outline justification
questions.why: The project brief consolidates early project definition and outline business justification for authorizing initiation.
optionWhy: The project brief consolidates early project definition and outline business justification for authorizing initiation.
The end project report evaluates delivered performance at project closure.
A checkpoint report concerns team progress on an authorized work package.
The quality register tracks quality checks after quality arrangements are planned.

questions.stem: The sponsoring business has a strategy to improve access to health services. How should a project benefit such as reduced waiting time be evaluated?
options: Only after any sustainability targets are removed
Against the business objective it is intended to contribute to
As equivalent to the physical equipment delivered
Only against the number of project team members
questions.why: Benefits should be measurable and show contribution to one or more business objectives.
optionWhy: Sustainability performance targets are a relevant constraint, not something to drop to measure benefits.
Benefits should be measurable and show contribution to one or more business objectives.
Equipment is an output; measurable wait-time reduction is a benefit from an outcome.
Team size may affect costs but cannot demonstrate the intended business improvement.

questions.stem: Which business case management step involves determining whether intended benefits have in fact been or will be realized?
questions.why: Confirm considers benefit realization, often through post-project reviews.
optionWhy: Assess is a named risk or issue activity, not one of the four business case steps.
Capture starts issue management rather than benefits confirmation.
Confirm considers benefit realization, often through post-project reviews.
Maintain updates justification as current forecasts and actuals change.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for maintaining sufficient ongoing commitment from people in the user community to adopt project products and realize benefits after closure?
questions.why: The senior user represents the user community and supports adoption and continued benefits realization.
optionWhy: The team manager delivers agreed work packages and normally has no overarching post-project benefits role.
Project support offers administrative and specialist support, not accountability for user benefits.
The senior supplier ensures supplier resources and technical quality, not primarily user adoption.
The senior user represents the user community and supports adoption and continued benefits realization.

questions.stem: A procurement-heavy project must document how supplier contracts and commercial arrangements will be managed. Where is this most appropriately covered?
questions.why: The commercial management approach in the PID covers commercial arrangements for the project.
optionWhy: The commercial management approach in the PID covers commercial arrangements for the project.
A risk register logs identified risks, not the project-wide commercial management approach.
The project product description defines overall deliverables and acceptance criteria.
The end project report summarizes delivery results at closure, too late to set contract management arrangements.

questions.stem: The board delegates independent checks of business, user and supplier concerns to qualified colleagues. What remains true?
options: Assurance becomes unnecessary once a supplier delivers
The board remains accountable for ensuring adequate project assurance
The project manager takes over board accountability
Project support must sign off every check as final authority
questions.why: The board may delegate assurance activity while retaining accountability for its appropriate performance.
optionWhy: Assurance continues to support effective governance across project lifecycle and concerns.
The board may delegate assurance activity while retaining accountability for its appropriate performance.
The project manager runs day-to-day delivery and cannot take over the board’s independent assurance accountability.
Project support should remain distinct from assurance to protect independence.

questions.stem: A team manager would benefit from a short plan showing how to organize and control an assigned work package. What kind of plan is this?
questions.why: A team plan is an optional plan to organize and control execution of a work package.
optionWhy: A project plan is the overall high-level view of delivery, timing and cost.
A stage plan is the project manager’s detailed basis for stage control.
A team plan is an optional plan to organize and control execution of a work package.
A benefits approach schedules reviews and actions for realizing outcomes, not team task control.

questions.stem: A project plan allows the team to deliver 5% fewer product units than forecast without exceeding its approved scope constraint. What is this permissible variation called?
questions.why: Scope tolerance defines the allowable variation in the products/deliverables included in a plan.
optionWhy: Risk appetite is willingness to pursue uncertain objectives, not a scope deviation limit.
Quality assurance is confidence in quality arrangements and does not define allowed product quantity variance.
Issue priority ranks required actions, not permitted scope changes.
Scope tolerance defines the allowable variation in the products/deliverables included in a plan.

questions.stem: A project manager determines the specialist equipment and staff effort needed to create products that have already been defined. Which part of planning is being performed?
questions.why: Preparing estimates identifies needed resources, effort and cost based on products and work.
optionWhy: Preparing estimates identifies needed resources, effort and cost based on products and work.
Confirming benefits concerns whether measurable improvements were realized.
The project board directs through authorizations and oversight rather than resource estimation detail.
Accepting products is a quality and handover activity, not estimating resources.

questions.stem: A project manager wants the current approval state and version of each planned product. Which record helps most?
questions.why: The product register maintains product status information, such as versions and approvals.
optionWhy: Checkpoint reports communicate work-package progress at intervals.
The product register maintains product status information, such as versions and approvals.
Business case is the ongoing investment justification, not the product status record.
The quality register captures quality activities and results, rather than the broad product approval status.

questions.stem: What BEST distinguishes a product requirement from a quality specification?
options: They are interchangeable terms with no different purpose
A requirement exists only in the issue register
A requirement states a documented need; a quality specification describes how it will be measured and the required level
Specifications refer exclusively to benefits after project closure
questions.why: Requirements state documented needs or expectations; quality specifications set measurable quality criteria and levels.
optionWhy: PRINCE2 distinguishes the need from the specific measures used to assess quality.
Requirements may be documented in approved management products; they are not restricted to the issue register.
Requirements state documented needs or expectations; quality specifications set measurable quality criteria and levels.
Quality specifications normally apply to products during their development or testing.

questions.stem: Which action supports accepting the overall project product rather than merely completing individual checks?
options: Treat any passing individual test as final user acceptance
Send a routine checkpoint report regardless of results
Apply agreed acceptance criteria and acceptance methods with the designated users
questions.why: Project product acceptance should follow the defined acceptance criteria, methods and authorized users.
optionWhy: A single passing test may not cover all project product acceptance conditions.
Change proposals need assessment and decision; automatic approval is unrelated to product acceptance.
Checkpoint reporting is useful for progress but is not proof of user acceptance.
Project product acceptance should follow the defined acceptance criteria, methods and authorized users.

questions.stem: A supplier might fail, but another supplier will be held on standby and engaged only if failure occurs. What is this response?
questions.why: A contingent plan identifies actions to take if the uncertain event occurs.
optionWhy: A contingent plan identifies actions to take if the uncertain event occurs.
Quality assurance addresses confidence in quality arrangements, not contingency response.
Exploit seeks to make a positive event happen rather than prepare a fallback for a threat.
Preparing a standby supplier is a deliberate risk response, not ignoring the uncertainty.

questions.stem: Which wording correctly distinguishes cause, event and effect in a risk description?
options: All three describe the same thing
Cause creates conditions; event is what may happen; effect describes the consequence for objectives
Cause is the project board; event is the issue register; effect is the work package
Cause is the uncertainty; event is the financial benefit; effect is who owns the project
questions.why: A useful risk statement connects the circumstances giving rise to the risk, the possible event and its effect on objectives.
optionWhy: Separating cause, uncertain event and objective effect improves assessment and response choice.
A useful risk statement connects the circumstances giving rise to the risk, the possible event and its effect on objectives.
Roles and registers are management elements, not risk cause/event/effect structure.
The event is the uncertain occurrence, while financial effects may or may not apply.

questions.stem: Decision-makers prefer the certainty of keeping an existing supplier even when evidence suggests a new supplier offers a better risk-adjusted result. Which bias may influence them?
questions.why: Loss aversion can lead people to overweight giving up something they already have relative to a potential gain.
optionWhy: Velocity describes how rapidly a risk would affect objectives if it occurred.
Exploitation is an active response to a positive opportunity, not the thinking pattern shown.
Loss aversion can lead people to overweight giving up something they already have relative to a potential gain.
Stage tolerance is a limit of delegated authority, not a cognitive bias.

questions.stem: A field-test failure has happened and requires an immediate repair; no approved scope revision is being proposed. Which issue class BEST fits?
questions.why: A problem/concern is an event already affecting or requiring consideration by the project.
optionWhy: The failure has already occurred, so it is not merely an uncertain future risk.
A request for change proposes alteration to a controlled baseline, which is not automatically the case here.
Opportunity responses address uncertain positive events, not a known test failure.
A problem/concern is an event already affecting or requiring consideration by the project.

questions.stem: A project has funds expressly reserved to cover authorized changes to product baselines. What are these funds called?
questions.why: The change budget is money or authorized constraints set aside for approved changes.
optionWhy: The change budget is money or authorized constraints set aside for approved changes.
Risk appetite expresses willingness to take risk, not a change funding provision.
Benefits tolerance sets limits on forecast benefit performance, not money earmarked for changes.
Stage boundary allowance is not the standard PRINCE2 term for authorized change funding.

questions.stem: The board is assessing stage results and deciding whether to authorize the next stage. Which report summarizes the just-completed stage for that decision?
questions.why: The end stage report summarizes stage performance and supports the board’s next-stage decision.
optionWhy: Issue reports concern particular issues rather than comprehensive stage performance.
The end stage report summarizes stage performance and supports the board’s next-stage decision.
Checkpoint reports communicate team work-package status to the project manager.
Highlight reports are periodic summaries during a stage, not the formal end-stage evaluation.

questions.stem: Which approach to data best supports effective progress management?
options: Collecting only historic data with no forecast
Replacing board decisions with automatically generated metrics
Using accurate actuals and trends to forecast remaining work and emerging exceptions
Recording every item manually regardless of usefulness
questions.why: Good data and systems support timely forecasting and sound management decisions.
optionWhy: Historic information matters, but PRINCE2 also requires forward-looking forecasts.
Metrics support, rather than replace, appropriate authority and management judgement.
Good data and systems support timely forecasting and sound management decisions.
Manual collection is not inherently better and may distract from useful analysis.

questions.stem: At the start of a project, which process is responsible for preparing the initial project brief and initiation stage plan?
questions.why: Starting up a project develops an early definition and plan to support initiation authorization.
optionWhy: Directing a project is where the board authorizes initiation, but it does not itself develop the brief.
Closing a project records acceptance, handover and final evaluation.
Managing a stage boundary prepares future stage or exception plans during an active project.
Starting up a project develops an early definition and plan to support initiation authorization.

questions.stem:
Which TWO statements are correct at a management stage boundary?
1. The project manager prepares information for the board.
2. The team manager alone authorizes the next stage.
3. The business case is checked for continued justification.
4. A new project mandate must be created for every stage.
questions.why: 1 and 3 are true: stage boundary planning and justification support the board’s stage authorization.
optionWhy: 1 and 3 are true: stage boundary planning and justification support the board’s stage authorization.
3 is true but 4 false: the original mandate commissions the project; it is not regenerated every stage.
Both 2 and 4 are false: new stages do not require new mandates or team-only authorizations.
1 is true but 2 false: the board, not the team manager, authorizes stages.

questions.stem: The project manager prepares a draft closure notification and confirms outstanding matters have owners. Which process is being used?
questions.why: Closing a project plans the controlled handover, notifications, lessons and recommendations for closure.

PRINCE2 principles remain applicable irrespective of this change in regulatory requirements.

questions.stem: A business case was compelling at authorization but costs now exceed the likely benefits. Which principle requires renewed justification?
questions.why: The project must remain worthwhile, not simply have had a good business case at its start.
optionWhy: This directs attention to the products and their quality rather than deciding whether continued investment is worthwhile.
The project must remain worthwhile, not simply have had a good business case at its start.
Lessons may inform the decision but do not replace the requirement for ongoing business justification.
Stages create decision points; it is the business justification principle that requires ongoing value.

questions.stem: A manager records an unexpected problem and alters the next stage approach after discussing what the team learned. Which principle is shown?
questions.why: Identifying and applying a lesson during the project demonstrates learning rather than filing lessons only at closure.
optionWhy: Exception control concerns delegated authority and forecasts against tolerances, not continuous learning.
A product focus defines the required outputs, but the scenario emphasizes changing future working based on experience.
Identifying and applying a lesson during the project demonstrates learning rather than filing lessons only at closure.
Tailoring adjusts the method to context; this change is specifically based on a captured lesson.

questions.stem: A small internal project has one person fulfilling both project support and team manager duties. Which statement best reflects tailoring?
options: This can be acceptable if responsibilities are clear and role constraints are respected
Every PRINCE2 role must be a different person
The project manager should also provide independent project assurance
The project may omit the business justification principle
questions.why: Some roles can be combined when suitable, but accountability and independence constraints must remain intact.
optionWhy: Some roles can be combined when suitable, but accountability and independence constraints must remain intact.
PRINCE2 permits suitable role combinations; a small team does not automatically require separate individuals for every role.
Project assurance must remain independent of the project manager and cannot simply be absorbed into that role.
All seven principles remain necessary even for a very small project.

questions.stem: The project board approves a stage plan and delegates delivery to the project manager within agreed bounds. Which principle primarily enables this?
questions.why: Tolerances provide boundaries within which lower levels can act without routine escalation.
optionWhy: Learning improves future decisions but does not establish the delegated authority in this scenario.
The plan should be product-focused, but the key is delegated decision rights.
Tailoring affects how procedures and documentation are applied, not the core authority mechanism described.
Tolerances provide boundaries within which lower levels can act without routine escalation.

questions.stem: Which project action most directly demonstrates the focus on products principle?
options: Start by listing team members’ favourite activities
Approve the supplier invoice before stating acceptance criteria
Define the required product and acceptance criteria before estimating tasks
Use the same report template for every stage regardless of need
questions.why: Starting with the result and its quality expectations keeps the project focused on deliverables.
optionWhy: Activity lists may be needed later, but they should flow from clearly defined required products.
Payments do not establish what products must be delivered or how they will be accepted.
Starting with the result and its quality expectations keeps the project focused on deliverables.
Rigid templates are not the essence of product focus and may obstruct appropriate tailoring.

questions.stem: Which action is consistent with tailoring while retaining PRINCE2?
options: Removing the manage by stages principle to save time
Using a concise combined digital management product with the required information
Allowing the project manager to act as their own independent assurance
Omitting approval for a new stage regardless of risk
questions.why: A documented product can be simplified or combined if control, information and accountability needs are satisfied.
optionWhy: Principles are universal and cannot be dropped under the pretext of tailoring.
A documented product can be simplified or combined if control, information and accountability needs are satisfied.
This breaks the independence of project assurance, not a permitted simplification.
Stage boundaries and control remain important; tailoring does not erase PRINCE2 governance.

questions.stem: The team discovers stakeholder responsibilities are unclear. Which principle most clearly addresses this?
questions.why: The principle requires defined accountabilities and effective relationships across the stakeholder interests.
optionWhy: Stages divide management decisions but do not themselves settle who is accountable for each activity.
Past lessons might help clarify responsibilities but are not the defining principle.
The principle requires defined accountabilities and effective relationships across the stakeholder interests.
A business case explains why to invest; it does not substitute for clear role definitions.

questions.stem: A project uses an iterative delivery method but retains board authorizations and clear tolerances. What is this an example of?
options: Replacing PRINCE2 with a software development methodology
Removing the directing a project process
Removing the focus on products principle
questions.why: The method can support different delivery approaches while retaining principles and accountability.
optionWhy: The method can support different delivery approaches while retaining principles and accountability.
An iterative delivery approach can coexist with PRINCE2 rather than replacing its governance.
The board must still make authorization and direction decisions, whatever delivery method is used.
Iterative delivery produces products too; it does not remove the need to define them.

questions.stem: Identify the missing words. A PRINCE2 project is planned, monitored and controlled on a ______ basis.
questions.why: Manage by stages gives the board controlled review and commitment points during the project.
optionWhy: The supplier delivers specialist products, but the governance principle does not describe supplier-only control.
The product register is a useful record; it is not the unit of stage-based management.
Reports may be periodic, but the principle is not tied to monthly scheduling.
Manage by stages gives the board controlled review and commitment points during the project.

questions.stem:
Which two actions demonstrate learning from experience?
1. Seek relevant lessons before initiation.
2. Wait until closure to record any lessons.
3. Update the next stage’s approach based on lessons learned.
4. Use only lessons from this project, never external ones.
questions.why: Both early use of lessons and applying lessons to later stages demonstrate continuous learning.
optionWhy: Seeking past lessons is right, but waiting until closure misses learning and improvement during delivery.
Both early use of lessons and applying lessons to later stages demonstrate continuous learning.
Neither postponing all learning nor refusing outside experience fits the principle.
Applying improvements is right, but lessons from other projects should not be ignored.

questions.stem: A system is delivered, but staff affected by it have not been trained and refuse to adopt it. What does this mainly illustrate?
options: The project should measure only product delivery
People affected by a project matter as well as those delivering it
Every affected person needs a seat on the project board
All benefits are guaranteed by product acceptance
questions.why: Managing change requires attention to the people who must work differently after handover.
optionWhy: The output alone is insufficient to ensure the change is adopted or benefits realized.
Managing change requires attention to the people who must work differently after handover.
Stakeholders must be engaged but need not all be board members.
Acceptance of the product does not guarantee its use or achievement of forecast benefits.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST distinguishes leadership from management in a project?
options: Leadership is budget control; management is motivating change
Management is unnecessary if leadership is strong
Leadership influences direction and commitment; management coordinates work and controls
Leadership belongs only to the project executive
questions.why: Leadership builds commitment to change while management plans, organizes and monitors delivery.
optionWhy: That reverses the broad distinction: management organizes and controls, while leadership creates direction and motivation.
Effective projects require both effective organization/control and purposeful direction.
Leadership builds commitment to change while management plans, organizes and monitors delivery.
People at different levels can demonstrate leadership, not only the board.

questions.stem: A project has a formal stakeholder list but no two-way conversations with affected teams. What is missing?
questions.why: Engagement involves listening and shaping the change, not just storing stakeholder names.
optionWhy: A plan describes work and control, but it cannot replace meaningful dialogue with those affected.
Product descriptions clarify quality and expectations; they are not a stakeholder engagement process.
An exception report addresses forecast tolerance breaches, not ongoing engagement.
Engagement involves listening and shaping the change, not just storing stakeholder names.

questions.stem: A charity project must send board updates by email, staff demos in person, and patient surveys online. Which PID approach specifies this mix of communication and feedback?
questions.why: It describes communication needs, channels, responsibilities, frequencies and feedback arrangements.
optionWhy: This sets quality standards and responsibilities, not the frequency and channels of stakeholder communication.
It describes communication needs, channels, responsibilities, frequencies and feedback arrangements.
This sets how uncertainties will be identified and handled; it does not govern general stakeholder communications.
A work package formally delegates specified product delivery work, not project-wide stakeholder engagement.

questions.stem: A department must adopt new working practices after a product is delivered. Where should planned activities to support this transition be described?
questions.why: This explains how changes to working practices and their adoption by affected people will be managed.
optionWhy: The product register records product status and information, not the people-focused adoption arrangements.
Lessons may be recorded about adoption, but planned transition actions belong in the change management approach.
This explains how changes to working practices and their adoption by affected people will be managed.
A resistance risk could be recorded there, but it is not the overall transition approach.

questions.stem: A team includes multiple languages and working cultures. Which capability most directly helps leaders collaborate effectively across these differences?
options: An extra management stage in every case
Removing remote workers from the team
questions.why: Understanding and working respectfully across cultural contexts supports effective diverse teams.
optionWhy: Understanding and working respectfully across cultural contexts supports effective diverse teams.
Exception reports concern forecast tolerance breaches, not basic team collaboration.
A stage boundary does not by itself improve cross-cultural relationships.
Eliminating diversity is not a PRINCE2 method for effective team management.

questions.stem: A team member can perform a task but does not have enough available hours for it. Which distinction matters?
questions.why: Capability concerns ability; capacity concerns available resources or time to do the work.
optionWhy: Capability concerns ability; capacity concerns available resources or time to do the work.
These both concern risk and do not explain the team member’s availability.
These concern planning levels, not the availability of qualified staff.
These distinguish delivered products from changes arising from their use, not staffing availability.

questions.stem: A distributed team argues about handover standards and deadlines. Which action best supports effective collaboration?
options: Keep team members apart and avoid discussing differences
Agree working practices, communication norms and interfaces together
Escalate every disagreement to the business layer
questions.why: Shared, explicit working practices and co-creation improve trust and coordination across locations.
optionWhy: Avoiding clarification leaves conflicting expectations and weakens trust.
Shared, explicit working practices and co-creation improve trust and coordination across locations.
The business layer does not manage every day-to-day working disagreement.
Quality criteria specify what the product must achieve; removing them is not a collaboration remedy.

questions.stem: A senior stakeholder announces a change without explaining why it matters to staff. Which leadership improvement is most relevant?
options: Increase the number of checkpoint reports
Replace the issue register with a spreadsheet
Explain the vision and involve affected people in the change
Ask project assurance to approve every team conversation
questions.why: Leadership helps people understand and support a future state rather than merely receive instructions.
optionWhy: Checkpoint reports track delegated delivery work, not the purpose people see in the change.
The recording format does not create commitment or understanding.
Leadership helps people understand and support a future state rather than merely receive instructions.
Assurance provides independent review, not approval of all dialogue.

questions.stem: Why is the change management approach relevant even when specialist products are technically complete?
options: It eliminates the need for user acceptance
It ensures all financial benefits arise instantly
It supports adoption of the new state and achievement of outcomes
questions.why: Delivered outputs create value only if people and operations use them to achieve intended change.
optionWhy: Technical products still need to satisfy requirements and appropriate acceptance.
Benefits may be realized long after the project closes and are not guaranteed by a document.
Business justification remains necessary regardless of how transition is planned.
Delivered outputs create value only if people and operations use them to achieve intended change.

questions.stem:
Which two practices make communication with stakeholders effective?
1. Match channels and frequency to stakeholder needs.
2. Send every stakeholder exactly the same technical detail.
3. Seek feedback and respond to it.
4. Restrict engagement to members of the project management team.
questions.why: Both appropriate communication design and two-way feedback support engagement and collaboration.
optionWhy: Matching needs is useful, but identical detail for every stakeholder ignores different interests and capabilities.
Uniform technical messages and exclusion of affected stakeholders would weaken engagement.
Both appropriate communication design and two-way feedback support engagement and collaboration.
Feedback helps, but stakeholders affected by the change may sit outside the project team.

questions.stem: Who may need to be engaged when project products change operational job roles?
options: Only the team members building the product
People working on the project and those affected by its change
questions.why: PRINCE2’s people element covers both the project ecosystem and stakeholders impacted by its outcomes.
optionWhy: The project manager coordinates work but is not the only person affected by operational changes.
Suppliers represent delivery needs; users and operational staff may be the most affected.
Building the product does not capture the needs of all people who must use or support it.
PRINCE2’s people element covers both the project ecosystem and stakeholders impacted by its outcomes.

questions.stem: A team member has technical expertise but repeatedly ignores agreed working practices. Which is the most complete way to view team effectiveness?
options: Consider skills, behaviours, relationships and working culture together
Ignore relationships as outside the project
Replace all team collaboration with formal reports
questions.why: Team effectiveness depends on more than specialist skill, including collaboration and the ability to work together.
optionWhy: Team effectiveness depends on more than specialist skill, including collaboration and the ability to work together.
Technical skill does not guarantee the required collaboration, behaviour or relationships.
Relationships are part of the people element and influence the success of change.
Formal reports do not remove the need for cooperative working and feedback.

questions.stem: A user group is influential but skeptical about a proposed new process. What is the best initial response?
options: Understand their concerns and involve them in shaping the change
Treat skepticism as proof of an exception situation
Ignore them because they are not on the project board
Record the group only in the risk register and stop communicating
questions.why: Engagement should be two-way and responsive to affected people’s motivations and needs.
optionWhy: Engagement should be two-way and responsive to affected people’s motivations and needs.
An exception is a forecast tolerance breach; concern from stakeholders does not automatically create one.
Stakeholders can affect project success even without formal board roles.
Resistance may create risks, but a risk register alone is not a stakeholder engagement strategy.

questions.stem: Identify the missing word. The ______ management approach in the PID describes how feedback is gathered and information shared with stakeholders.
questions.why: The communication management approach defines who needs information, how it will be communicated and when.
optionWhy: The benefits management approach addresses benefit reviews and realization, not general communication arrangements.
The commercial management approach addresses commercial relationships and supplier arrangements.
The communication management approach defines who needs information, how it will be communicated and when.
The quality management approach focuses on verifying product quality against requirements.

questions.stem:
Project staff understand what to build but do not know how the organization will change after delivery. Which two actions help most?
1. Describe the current and target operating states.
2. Treat organizational adoption as outside project concerns.
3. Plan transition and communication with affected users.
4. Measure project success only by completion of technical work.
questions.why: A clear desired future state and planned transition/engagement help people make the change.
optionWhy: Understanding the transition is useful, but dismissing adoption contradicts the people element.
A clear desired future state and planned transition/engagement help people make the change.
Ignoring adoption and measuring only outputs overlooks whether outcomes and benefits occur.
Transition planning helps, but technical completion alone is not sufficient to show change success.

questions.stem: A team has specialists with strong individual skills but poor cooperation. What is the most likely gap?
options: Team cohesion and effective working relationships
questions.why: Individual skills alone do not create trust, shared goals or coordinated delivery.
optionWhy: A product register is useful, but the description concerns how people work together.
Individual skills alone do not create trust, shared goals or coordinated delivery.
Tolerance limits define authority; they do not themselves create collaborative working.
The business case is about investment justification, not the direct team behaviour gap.

questions.stem: A new booking system is delivered to a hospital. Patients then book appointments online. Which is the outcome?
options: A measured reduction of 20 minutes per call
questions.why: An outcome is the change in real-world behaviour following use of the delivered outputs.
optionWhy: The system itself is an output; it does not describe the resulting change in behaviour.
An outcome is the change in real-world behaviour following use of the delivered outputs.
The quantified improvement is a benefit resulting from the changed behaviour.
This management product defines the required project product and its acceptance, not the outcome.

questions.stem: A project replaces travel with video meetings, reducing costs but also reducing local café revenue. What is the café revenue reduction from the investing organization’s perspective if recognized as an expected negative effect?
questions.why: A dis-benefit is a measurable decline from an outcome, perceived as negative by the investing organization.
optionWhy: An output is a product delivered by the project, not a negative measurable consequence.
A benefit is a measurable improvement valued by the investing organization, not a decline perceived as negative.
This is a management record, not the name of an expected measurable decline.
A dis-benefit is a measurable decline from an outcome, perceived as negative by the investing organization.

questions.stem: A project is likely to finish on time but planned operational savings may only arrive two years later. Which approach identifies how the savings will be reviewed after closure?
questions.why: This defines benefit reviews, responsible parties and management actions for realizing benefits, including post-project reviews.
optionWhy: This defines benefit reviews, responsible parties and management actions for realizing benefits, including post-project reviews.
A checkpoint report provides progress on a work package, not a plan for long-term benefit reviews.
The project product description sets the whole project product’s quality and acceptance criteria, not benefits review scheduling.
This escalates forecast tolerance breaches rather than scheduling routine realization measurements.

questions.stem: Which PID approach defines how sustainability targets will be reviewed and controlled?
questions.why: It identifies actions, reviews and controls to meet agreed sustainability performance targets.
optionWhy: Commercial management addresses contractual and supplier relationships, not the primary sustainability controls.
Communication arrangements can report sustainability information but do not themselves define its performance controls.
It identifies actions, reviews and controls to meet agreed sustainability performance targets.
A sustainability-related uncertainty may be recorded as a risk, but this is not the sustainability approach.

questions.stem: At a stage boundary the business case is updated using actual expenditure and revised benefits. What is the main reason?
options: To support a fresh decision on continued investment
To prove all forecast benefits have already been realized
To authorize the team manager to approve the entire project
questions.why: The board needs current cost, risk and benefit forecasts rather than relying solely on assumptions made at initiation.
optionWhy: The board needs current cost, risk and benefit forecasts rather than relying solely on assumptions made at initiation.
Benefits may occur after closure; a stage boundary does not automatically prove their realization.
The business case justifies investment and does not replace product-level definitions.
Project authorization is a directing-level decision, not an automatic result of updating the business case.

questions.stem: Identify the missing word. In the business case technique, ______ means keeping the business case current with actual and forecast information.
questions.why: Maintain keeps the business case updated as the project progresses and information changes.
optionWhy: Confirm relates to checking achieved benefits, not generally updating the case during delivery.
Maintain keeps the business case updated as the project progresses and information changes.
Develop establishes the case and the information used for investment decisions.
Check tests whether justification remains valid; maintenance changes the current case.

questions.stem: Which activity is closest to the CHECK step of business case management?
options: Assess whether remaining cost and risk are justified by expected value
questions.why: Checking the business case tests whether further investment remains desirable, viable and achievable.
optionWhy: Time recording may inform planning but does not itself check continuing business justification.
Product descriptions define deliverables and quality, not directly the desirability of investment.
This supports risk control, not checking the overall case for continued investment.
Checking the business case tests whether further investment remains desirable, viable and achievable.

questions.stem: A project product will be delivered successfully, but the proposed outcome no longer supports the organization’s strategy. What should be revisited?
options: Business case alignment with business objectives
Only the team members’ work instructions
questions.why: Investment needs to remain justified by expected benefits and their contribution to business objectives.
optionWhy: Reporting frequency will not repair a loss of strategic justification.
Successful quality activities do not prove that the outcome is still strategically valuable.
Investment needs to remain justified by expected benefits and their contribution to business objectives.
Work instructions do not resolve whether the project remains worthwhile.

questions.stem:
Which two statements about outputs, outcomes and benefits are CORRECT?
1. A specialist deliverable can be an output.
2. Every output automatically guarantees a benefit.
3. Changed operational behaviour can be an outcome.
4. Benefits can never be measured after closure.
questions.why: Outputs are what gets delivered; outcomes are changes that arise when outputs are used.
optionWhy: A specialist deliverable is an output, but benefits are not guaranteed just by producing it.
Outputs do not guarantee benefits, and many benefits are reviewed after closure.
Outputs are what gets delivered; outcomes are changes that arise when outputs are used.
Changed behaviour is an outcome, but benefits can be measured after the project has ended.

questions.stem: During pre-project work, a small amount of justification is assembled before full initiation. Which management product best captures this initial rationale and scope?
questions.why: The project brief gives a common starting point and can include the outline business case before detailed initiation.
optionWhy: The project brief gives a common starting point and can include the outline business case before detailed initiation.
An end project report evaluates completed project performance rather than setting up the initial case.
This tracks delivery progress on a work package, which has not yet been authorized.
Lessons may be consulted, but the lessons report does not establish the outline case and starting scope.

questions.stem: A project’s senior user requests a feature while the senior supplier worries about technical feasibility. What are these roles representing?
options: User need and supplier delivery capability respectively
The board and the project manager respectively
Quality assurance and project assurance respectively
questions.why: Senior users represent requirements and benefits; senior suppliers represent resources and technical feasibility.
optionWhy: The business viewpoint is represented by the executive; user and supplier interests have different concerns.
Senior users represent requirements and benefits; senior suppliers represent resources and technical feasibility.
Both senior user and senior supplier normally sit on the project board and are not the project manager.
These are assurance concepts, not the three project interests represented by the board.

questions.stem: The project needs to define contracts, procurement relationships and how suppliers will be managed commercially. Which PID product is most relevant?
questions.why: This records how commercial relationships, agreements and supplier arrangements are managed.
optionWhy: Lessons can inform procurement decisions but do not establish the project’s commercial arrangements.
This plans outcomes and benefit realization, not the contractual arrangements.
This records how commercial relationships, agreements and supplier arrangements are managed.
The quality register records quality checks and their results, rather than commercial governance.

questions.stem: A product depends on two specialist teams. Which organizing aid best breaks the delivery work into manageable work elements?
questions.why: A work breakdown structure decomposes the work needed to deliver products and helps organize responsibilities.
optionWhy: A work breakdown structure decomposes the work needed to deliver products and helps organize responsibilities.
The risk register records uncertain threats and opportunities, not a breakdown of activities or work.
This summarizes project performance at completion, not planned work division.
This reports a forecast breach of tolerance, not routine breakdown of delivery work.

questions.stem: Which role remains ultimately accountable for the project’s business case and success?
questions.why: The executive is the single point of accountability and owns the project’s business justification.
optionWhy: Project support supplies administrative and specialist support but is not the overall accountable owner.
The senior supplier represents delivery capability and technical integrity, not overall business accountability.
The project manager manages day-to-day work under board direction; overall accountability lies above that role.
The executive is the single point of accountability and owns the project’s business justification.

questions.stem: A supplier cannot provide the specialist test staff promised for the project. Which project board role should address supplier capacity?
questions.why: The senior supplier is responsible for representing and securing supplier resources and technical capability.
optionWhy: The senior user represents user requirements and benefits, rather than securing supplier expertise.
The senior supplier is responsible for representing and securing supplier resources and technical capability.
Project support may assist administration but is not the board representative for supplier capability.
The executive owns overall justification but specialist supplier commitment is the senior supplier’s focus.

questions.stem: A project manager has sufficient specialist knowledge and wants to manage a small team directly. Which role may they also undertake?
questions.why: The project manager can perform team-manager responsibilities where scale, skills and capacity make this suitable.
optionWhy: The executive is a separate governing role and must not be combined with project manager.
Project assurance must remain independent of the project manager.
The project manager can perform team-manager responsibilities where scale, skills and capacity make this suitable.
The senior user is a board role representing users and is not combined with the project manager.

questions.stem: Which PID product makes clear who has authority and responsibilities in the project management team?
options: Project management team structure and role descriptions
questions.why: The structure and role descriptions show the roles, responsibilities and reporting relationships.
optionWhy: The risk register records individual risks and risk owners, not the entire management structure.
The quality register records planned and completed quality activities, not all governance roles.
This records products and their status, not the decision rights of the project management team.
The structure and role descriptions show the roles, responsibilities and reporting relationships.

questions.stem: The project board has delegated authority to approve certain changes to a named person. Which role has been established?
questions.why: A change authority decides specified requests within limits delegated by the project board.
optionWhy: A change authority decides specified requests within limits delegated by the project board.
A risk action owner carries out a particular response action; they do not receive general change approval rights.
A quality reviewer checks products against criteria but does not automatically authorize changes to baselines.
Assurance independently checks governance and quality but is not synonymous with delegated change approval.

questions.stem: Which step is most relevant when a project reviews who its affected external parties are before designing governance?
questions.why: The organizing technique begins by considering the relevant business, user, supplier and wider relationships.
optionWhy: The end project report is produced near closure, not while designing the initial organizational ecosystem.
The organizing technique begins by considering the relevant business, user, supplier and wider relationships.
A team plan addresses the detailed work of a delivery team, not the broad stakeholder ecosystem.
Quality inspections do not map the full organizational relationships around the project.

questions.stem: The project board wants independent checks but asks the project manager to provide their own assurance. Why is this inappropriate?
options: The project manager is too busy to write reports
All assurance must be done by an external certification body
Project assurance must remain independent of the project manager
Assurance is only needed after closure
questions.why: The board retains accountability for assurance and must maintain an independent line of review.
optionWhy: Workload alone is not the governance reason; independence is the fundamental requirement.
Project assurance can be delegated within the project team if independent of the project manager.
The board retains accountability for assurance and must maintain an independent line of review.
Assurance supports the board during project delivery, not just at the end.

questions.stem: A plan shows that testing cannot start until configuration is complete. What planning concept is described?
questions.why: A dependency is a relationship in which one work item or product relies on another.
optionWhy: Sustainability targets concern environmental or social performance, not the order of activities.
A risk budget funds responses to uncertainty, not the logical relationship between tasks.
A quality specification defines measurable quality requirements, not task sequencing.
A dependency is a relationship in which one work item or product relies on another.

questions.stem: Which management product formally tells a delivery team which products to create and the applicable constraints?
questions.why: It describes the delegated delivery, products, constraints, reporting and acceptance requirements.
optionWhy: The project brief captures the initial project definition before initiation; it does not allocate specific delivery work.
It describes the delegated delivery, products, constraints, reporting and acceptance requirements.
An end stage report evaluates completed stage performance for the board.
An exception report escalates a forecast tolerance breach rather than authorizing ordinary work.

questions.stem: A project is planned in detail for the next stage but only in outline for much later stages. Which concept supports this?
questions.why: Planning detail should reflect the available certainty; near work can be planned more precisely.
optionWhy: The daily log records informal issues and day-to-day notes; it does not govern future planning detail.
Assurance reviews governance but does not define the planning horizon principle.
Planning detail should reflect the available certainty; near work can be planned more precisely.
Exception management responds to forecast tolerance breaches rather than governing planning detail by horizon.

questions.stem: Which statement distinguishes a project plan from a stage plan?
options: The project plan gives the high-level overall picture; a stage plan gives detailed control for one stage
A stage plan replaces the project plan for the whole project
Only the team manager uses a project plan
A project plan is always produced after the final stage
questions.why: The plans serve different management levels and planning horizons.
optionWhy: The plans serve different management levels and planning horizons.
The project plan remains the overall baseline; a stage plan covers a management stage.
The project board uses the project plan for overall monitoring, while the project manager controls stages.
The project plan is assembled during initiation and updated throughout the project.

questions.stem: An approved stage plan can no longer deliver within tolerance. The board asks for a replacement plan. What type is prepared?
questions.why: An approved exception plan replaces the stage or project plan for the period it covers.
optionWhy: A team plan governs delivery of a team’s work package, not the replacement of a breached stage plan.
This defines how benefits will be realized and measured, not the revised stage control plan.
The project brief captures initial scope and justification, not exception recovery plans.
An approved exception plan replaces the stage or project plan for the period it covers.

questions.stem: A project manager starts planning by defining deliverables before listing activities. Which technique does this illustrate?
questions.why: Defining and analysing products first is central to PRINCE2 planning.
optionWhy: Defining and analysing products first is central to PRINCE2 planning.
Risk exposure measures potential effects of uncertainty rather than identifying required products.
Exception management concerns forecasts against tolerances, not the initial product-led planning method.
Quality control tests products against criteria; it is not the technique for creating the plan.
